```javascript
}

function runQueryEngineQASuite() {
  const tests = [
    testRoleResolutionTiers,
    testRawStringPreservation,
    testNoWorldwideImplicitly,
    testWorldwideOnlyWhenExplicit,
    testMultipleRegionsProduceExactCount,
    testUnresolvedRegionDoesNotBecomeWorldwide,
    testCountryTargetDistinction,
    testDefaultTargetCountryFromUserCountry,
    testFreshnessInvalidReasons,
    testFreshnessValid,
    testAllStrategiesShareSchema,
    testNoDuplicateStrategySignatures,
    testPlanCanonicalRoleInvariant,
    testSiteSyntax,
    testAshbyStrategyPresent,
    testGoogleQueriesDoNotContainCanonicalIDs,
    testRemoteDoesNotCreateWorldwide,
    testNoSkillsMeansNoSkillsLed,
    testInvalidRemoteFailsClosed,
    testApplicationAutomationProhibited,
    testStructuredRetrievalContext,
    testProductionLikePlan
  ];

  const results = [];
  let failures = 0;

  tests.forEach(testFn => {
    try {
      const result = testFn();
      results.push({ test: testFn.name, status: result });
      Logger.log('PASS: ' + testFn.name);
    } catch (error) {
      failures++;
      results.push({
        test: testFn.name,
        status: 'FAIL',
        error: String(error && error.stack ? error.stack : error)
      });
      Logger.log('FAIL: ' + testFn.name + ' :: ' + String(error));
    }
  });

  Logger.log('==============================================');
  Logger.log('G2 QUERY INTELLIGENCE QA SUITE');
  Logger.log('Tests: ' + tests.length);
  Logger.log('Failures: ' + failures);
  Logger.log('Status: ' + (failures === 0 ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'));
  Logger.log('==============================================');

  if (failures > 0) {
    throw new Error('G2 QA SUITE FAILED: ' + failures + ' test(s) failed.');
  }

  return {
    status: 'PASS',
    testsRun: tests.length,
    failures: 0,
    results: results
  };
}

function testQueryEngine() {
  return runQueryEngineQASuite();
}
```

---

# 20. WHY THIS TEST SUITE IS DIFFERENT FROM THE ORIGINAL G2 TEST

The original G2 draft relied mainly on a single sample execution and log inspection. That is not sufficient for the frozen architecture.

The final suite checks behavior and invariants, including:

```text
Role resolution tiers
Raw-value preservation
No implicit Worldwide
Explicit Worldwide
Multiple regions
Unresolved geography
User country vs target country
Default target country traceability
Invalid freshness reasons
Valid freshness
Common strategy schema
Duplicate signatures
Plan canonical role
Google syntax
Ashby inclusion
No private canonical IDs in queries
Remote/worldwide separation
No skills-led strategy without skills
Invalid remote fail-closed behavior
Application automation prohibition
Retrieval context completeness
Production-like plan
```

This is the appropriate level for a gate that feeds G3.

# 25. REQUIRED ADVERSARIAL TEST MATRIX

These are the minimum manual spot checks after the automated suite.

| Case | Input condition | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| A | Nigeria + Fully Remote | No Worldwide strategy unless `allowWorldwide=true` |
| B | Nigeria + Africa | Country + Africa region strategy |
| C | Nigeria + Africa + EMEA | Two separate region strategies |
| D | `allowWorldwide=true` | One explicit Worldwide strategy |
| E | No keywords | No `SKILLS_LED` strategy |
| F | Product Operations | Controlled Product Operations taxonomy |
| G | Related title | `RELATED_TITLE` resolution, not custom |
| H | Adjacent title | `ADJACENT_ROLE` resolution, visibly distinct |
| I | Custom role | `CUSTOM_ROLE` resolution |
| J | Invalid freshness `0` | Invalid plan with `FRESHNESS_OUT_OF_RANGE_1_TO_90` |
| K | Invalid freshness `91` | Invalid plan with same range reason |
| L | Invalid freshness `abc` | `FRESHNESS_NOT_NUMERIC` |
| M | String regions `Africa, EMEA` | Raw value remains string; canonical list contains two regions |
| N | `country=Nigeria`, `targetCountries=Germany` | User country Nigeria; target country Germany |
| O | Unknown region | Warning; no automatic Worldwide |
| P | Google query inspection | No `site://` or `site:://` |
| Q | Query inspection | No internal Plan ID in search text |
| R | ATS inspection | Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby strategy declarations exist |

# 26. QUERY PLAN EXAMPLE

For:

```javascript
{
  role: 'Operations Specialist',
  country: 'Nigeria',
  regions: ['Africa', 'EMEA'],
  remotePreference: 'Fully Remote',
  keywords: ['Excel', 'Automation'],
  exclusions: ['US-only', 'Canada-only'],
  freshnessDays: 7,
  allowWorldwide: false
}
```

the plan should conceptually contain:

```text
EXACT_ROLE_COUNTRY_NIGERIA
EXACT_ROLE_REGION_AFRICA
EXACT_ROLE_REGION_EMEA
FAMILY_COUNTRY_NIGERIA
SKILLS_LED
ATS_API_GREENHOUSE
ATS_API_LEVER
ATS_API_ASHBY
```

There is **no** `WORLDWIDE_EXPLICIT` strategy because Worldwide was not explicitly requested.

The exact plan remains machine-readable rather than depending on this human-readable list.

---

# 27. GOOGLE QUERY EXAMPLES

A typical exact-country query may look like:

```text
"Operations Specialist" ("Nigeria") (remote OR "work from anywhere" OR "work remotely") ("Excel" OR "Automation") -"US-only" -"Canada-only"
```

A regional query may look like:

```text
"Operations Specialist" Africa (remote OR "work from anywhere" OR "work remotely") ("Excel" OR "Automation") -"US-only" -"Canada-only"
```

A skills-led query may look like:

```text
Nigeria (remote OR "work from anywhere" OR "work remotely") ("Excel" OR "Automation") -"US-only" -"Canada-only"
```

A worldwide query is only rendered when explicitly requested.

A structured ATS strategy does not need a Google query because G3 will use the source-specific endpoint mode.

---

# 28. WHY FRESHNESS IS STORED BUT NOT FAKED INTO GOOGLE SYNTAX

The user's freshness preference belongs in the structured plan:

```javascript
freshnessDays: 7
```

and in retrieval context:

```javascript
requestedFreshnessDays: 7
```

This is safer than pretending that a generic Google text string such as:

```text
after:2026-09-02
```

is a universal guarantee of posting freshness across all sources.

G3 is responsible for source-aware date interpretation and final job-level freshness.

The master manual explicitly requires freshness to be a separate dimension from eligibility and source reliability. fileciteturn12file1L129-L138

---

# 29. WHY REMOTE DOES NOT MEAN WORLDWIDE

This rule is central to the project.

A role may be:

```text
Remote
```

but restricted to:

```text
United States only
```

or:

```text
EU only
```

or:

```text
EMEA
```

or:

```text
Americas
```

Therefore the Query Plan must keep:

```text
remote = Fully Remote
```

separate from:

```text
geography = Nigeria / Africa / EMEA / Worldwide
```

This is also why G4/G5 later require job-level evidence and eligibility evaluation rather than assuming the query itself proves eligibility.

---

# 30. WHY G2 DOES NOT CLAIM NIGERIA ELIGIBILITY

G2 can express a search intent:

```text
Nigeria
```

It cannot prove:

```text
Nigeria eligible
```

That proof comes later from the actual source evidence attached to an individual job.

The Phase 4 rules require evidence before claiming Nigeria eligibility. fileciteturn12file1L140-L150

---

# 31. PERCHANCE INTERFACE BOUNDARY

The prior G2 work explored a Perchance front door. The final architecture keeps the intelligence logic centralized.

A front end may collect:

```text
Role
Country
Target countries
Regions
Remote preference
Employment type
Keywords / skills
Exclusions
Freshness
Worldwide permission
Work authorization
Timezone
Mode
```

and submit them as the input object.

The front end must **not** maintain a second independent copy of the role taxonomy or strategy-generation logic.

The previous G2 draft explicitly identified a problem with duplicated intelligence in Perchance. The final rule is:

```text
UI = input collection / presentation
Apps Script = canonical Query Intelligence
```

## 31.1 No second intelligence engine

Do not hard-code a separate Perchance list like:

```javascript
strategies: [
  { id: 'exact', ... },
  { id: 'synonym', ... }
]
```

while Apps Script has another strategy model.

That would create two sources of truth.

## 31.2 G2 web deployment boundary

Do not make the G2 implementation depend on a public Apps Script web app solely to prove that the logic works.

The logic can be unit-tested inside Apps Script first.

A public endpoint can be introduced later as part of the G3/backend integration when source discovery and authentication/rate-limit design justify it.

```text
QUERY PLAN

Role

STRATEGIES
```

rather than appearing as a hidden default.

# 33. AUDIT LOGGING

G2 itself does not need to write every Query Plan body into `AUDIT_LOG`, because that may create oversized operational records.

However, successful QA execution may be recorded with a compact event such as:

```javascript
function logG2QASuccess(result) {
  if (typeof logEvent !== 'function') return;

  logEvent(
    'G2_QUERY_ENGINE_QA_PASS',
    'G2 QA suite passed. Tests=' + result.testsRun + '; failures=' + result.failures,
    'INFO'
  );
}
```

Do not call the function unless the existing `Logger.gs` contract is confirmed.

The execution evidence itself should be retained outside the production data tables if necessary.

The earlier Phase 4 baseline already used `AUDIT_LOG` for traceability, so this remains compatible with the existing operational model. fileciteturn14file1L576-L585

# 37. FAILURE MODES AND RECOVERY

## 37.1 Syntax error after paste

Stop.

Check:

- unmatched braces;
- smart quotes accidentally pasted from a word processor;
- duplicate `const` declarations;
- missing commas;
- unsupported syntax from a malformed copy.

Run the Apps Script editor's syntax check again.

## 37.2 `Identifier has already been declared`

This usually means that the same constant exists in two files.

Search for:

```text
ROLE_TAXONOMY
COUNTRY_MODEL
REGION_MODEL
REMOTE_TYPES
ATS_SOURCES
QUERY_SCHEMA_VERSION
```

Keep one canonical definition.

## 37.3 Tests report duplicate strategy signature

Do not simply remove the test.

Inspect the conflicting strategies and determine whether two semantic strategies are actually identical.

The correct fix is to change the generation logic so different strategies differ semantically, or remove the redundant strategy.

## 37.4 Tests report wrong region count

Inspect:

```text
inputs.regions
geographyResolution.regions.canonical
EXACT_ROLE_REGION strategies
```

Do not revert to first-region-only behavior.

## 37.5 Test says Worldwide appeared unexpectedly

Search for any remaining code like:

```javascript
if (remote === 'Fully Remote') ... Worldwide ...
```

Remove the implicit fallback.

## 37.6 Test says raw string became an array

Inspect the object under:

```text
userIntent.raw
```

Raw fields must mirror the supplied type.

Canonical arrays belong under `userIntent.canonical`.

## 37.7 Freshness test fails

Inspect the exact reason:

```text
FRESHNESS_NOT_NUMERIC
FRESHNESS_NOT_INTEGER
FRESHNESS_OUT_OF_RANGE_1_TO_90
```

Do not silently replace invalid input with 7.

## 37.8 Test says user country and target country are conflated

Confirm whether `targetCountries` was explicitly supplied.

Expected source values:

```text
EXPLICIT
DEFAULTED_FROM_USER_COUNTRY
NONE
```

# 40. FORMAL G2 EXIT CRITERIA

G2 is eligible for a PASS decision only when all of the following are true:

```text
1. QueryEngine.gs exists and loads without syntax error.
2. QueryEngineTests.gs exists and loads without syntax error.
3. All automated G2 QA tests pass.
4. No duplicate strategy signatures exist in a production-like plan.
5. Every strategy satisfies the mandatory schema.
6. Plan-level canonical role invariant passes.
7. Every resolved input region creates exactly one exact region strategy.
8. Worldwide is generated only when explicitly authorized.
9. Raw input values retain their original scalar/array semantics.
10. Invalid freshness values produce precise validation reasons.
11. User country is distinguishable from target opportunity countries.
12. Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby structured strategies exist.
13. Google queries contain valid `site:` syntax where applicable.
14. Internal canonical identifiers do not appear in Google search text.
15. The plan carries retrieval context required by G3.
16. The plan is JSON serializable.
17. `compatibleWith` includes `G3`.
18. No automatic job application behavior exists.
19. A rollback point exists.
20. Execution evidence is retained.
```

If any one of these is not evidenced, G2 remains **NOT YET VERIFIED**.

---

# 41. G3 HANDOFF CONTRACT

Once the G2 exit criteria are met, G3 may treat the following fields as stable interfaces:

```javascript
plan.schemaVersion
plan.taxonomyVersion
plan.geographyVersion
plan.planId
plan.generatedAt
plan.compatibleWith
plan.status
plan.executable
plan.userIntent
plan.retrievalContext
plan.geographyResolution
plan.strategies
plan.totalStrategies
plan.validation
```

G3 should iterate over:

```javascript
plan.strategies
```

and choose adapters based on:

```javascript
strategy.kind
strategy.sourceType
strategy.retrieval
strategy.geography
strategy.roleResolution
```

G3 should not parse the human-readable query string to reconstruct semantics that already exist in the structured object.

---

# 42. G3 MUST NOT ASSUME FROM G2

G3 must not assume:

```text
query found = job is live
remote = worldwide
country phrase = hiring eligibility
source page = verified employer page
search result = current posting
query terms = evidence
```

Those are later verification questions.

The Phase 4 design explicitly separates discovery, evidence, eligibility, freshness and source reliability. fileciteturn12file1L129-L139

---

# 43. VERSIONING POLICY

The current frozen values are:

```text
Query schema:    2.1
Taxonomy:        1.0
Geography:       1.0
ATS endpoint:    PUBLIC_JOB_POSTINGS_API
G3 compatibility: yes
```

Increment the schema version when a breaking structural change occurs.

Increment the taxonomy version when role semantics change materially.

Increment the geography version when the canonical geography contract changes materially.

Do not increment versions merely because a code comment changes.

---

# 44. CHANGE CONTROL AFTER FREEZE

Once G2 is frozen, future improvements should be handled as controlled changes rather than silent edits.

Example:

```text
G2.1.1 — defect fix, same contract
G2.1.2 — taxonomy clarification, same contract
G2.2   — additive non-breaking schema extension
G3     — source discovery layer consuming G2
```

Avoid changing the meaning of existing strategy IDs after G3 starts consuming them.

---

# 45. WHAT NOT TO DO AFTER THIS DOCUMENT

Do not reopen the old query-generator architecture merely because the final module looks more sophisticated.

Do not reintroduce:

- implicit Worldwide expansion;
- first-region-only logic;
- naive role substring matching;
- duplicate intelligence inside Perchance;
- raw-value type coercion for convenience;
- strategy generation without schema validation;
- duplicate semantic strategies;
- fabricated ATS calls;
- fake freshness guarantees;
- job-level eligibility conclusions inside G2.

The purpose of these patches is to make the existing corrected design reliable enough to hand to G3, not to start another redesign cycle.

# 47. FINAL DECISION STATEMENT

The final G2 architecture is:

```text
User Intent
    ↓
Query Engine
    ├── Role Taxonomy
    ├── Country Model
    ├── Region Model
    ├── Remote Model
    ├── Freshness Validation
    ├── Raw/Canonical Separation
    ├── Strategy Generator
    ├── Strategy Schema Validator
    ├── Duplicate Signature Validator
    └── Versioned Query Plan
             ↓
            G3
```

The critical quality properties are:

```text
DETERMINISTIC
AUDITABLE
VERSIONED
FAIL-CLOSED
NO-FABRICATION
NO-IMPLICIT-WORLDWIDE
NO-ROLE-GUESSING
NO-REGION-GUESSING
NO-DUPLICATE-STRATEGIES
NO-HIDDEN-SECOND-ENGINE
NO-AUTOMATIC-APPLICATIONS
G3-COMPATIBLE
```

This document therefore represents the **final corrected G2 implementation baseline** to be executed and evidenced in the actual Apps Script environment.

```markdown
**Success Check:** Running the test function produces valid query strings with no syntax errors (e.g., no `site:://`).

## Step 2 – Create the new module: `QueryEngine.gs`

- In the Apps Script editor, click the **`+`** icon next to **Files** (left panel) → **Script**.
- Name the new file: **`QueryEngine.gs`**
- Copy and paste the following code exactly:

javascript

```
// ============================================================================
// QUERYENGINE.GS – Phase 4A Query Intelligence
// Generates structured search queries from user profile inputs.
// ============================================================================

/**
 * Main function to generate search query variants.
 * @param {Object} params - Input parameters.
 * @param {string} params.role - Target role (e.g., "Operations Specialist").
 * @param {string} params.country - User's country (e.g., "Nigeria").
 * @param {string} params.remote - "Fully Remote", "Hybrid", or "On-site".
 * @param {string} params.regions - Comma-separated regions (e.g., "Africa,EMEA").
 * @param {Array<string>} params.exclusions - Array of phrases to exclude (e.g., ["US-only", "Canada-only"]).
 * @param {string} params.keywords - Additional skill or tool keywords.
 * @param {number} params.freshness - Preferred days since posting (not used in search string yet, but stored).
 * @returns {Object} { variants: string[], structured: Object }
 */
function generateQueries(params) {
  // 1. Normalize inputs
  const role = params.role || '';
  const country = params.country || 'Nigeria';
  const remote = params.remote || 'Fully Remote';
  const regions = params.regions ? params.regions.split(',').map(r => r.trim()) : [];
  const exclusions = params.exclusions || ['US-only', 'Canada-only', 'UK-only'];
  const keywords = params.keywords || '';
  const sources = ['greenhouse.io', 'lever.co', 'workable.com']; // From G1 sources

  // 2. Build role family synonyms (expand 'Operations' to common variants)
  let roleTerms = [role];
  const lowerRole = role.toLowerCase();
  if (lowerRole.includes('operations')) {
    roleTerms.push('Operations Specialist', 'Operations Associate', 'Operations Analyst', 'Business Operations');
  } else if (lowerRole.includes('product')) {
    roleTerms.push('Product Operations', 'Product Specialist');
  } else if (lowerRole.includes('support')) {
    roleTerms.push('Customer Support', 'Technical Support', 'Support Operations');
  }
  // Deduplicate and preserve order
  const uniqueRoles = [...new Set(roleTerms)];
  const roleQuery = '(' + uniqueRoles.join(' OR ') + ')';

  // 3. Build geography query
  let geoTerms = [country];
  regions.forEach(r => geoTerms.push(r));
  // If 'Worldwide' is not in the list, add it as a broad fallback (only if remote is fully remote)
  if (remote === 'Fully Remote' && !geoTerms.includes('Worldwide')) {
    geoTerms.push('Worldwide');
  }
  const geoQuery = '(' + geoTerms.join(' OR ') + ')';

  // 4. Build remote query
  let remoteQuery = '';
  if (remote === 'Fully Remote') {
    remoteQuery = '(remote OR "work from anywhere" OR worldwide OR "anywhere")';
  } else if (remote === 'Hybrid') {
    remoteQuery = '(hybrid OR remote)';
  } else {
    remoteQuery = '(on-site OR onsite)';
  }

  // 5. Build exclusions
  let exclusionQuery = '';
  if (exclusions.length > 0) {
    exclusionQuery = '-' + exclusions.join(' -');
  }

  // 6. Keywords
  let keywordQuery = keywords.trim() || '';

  // 7. Source constraints (site:domain)
  let sourceQuery = '(' + sources.map(s => 'site:' + s).join(' OR ') + ')';

  // 8. Assemble primary query
  let parts = [roleQuery, geoQuery, remoteQuery];
  if (keywordQuery) parts.push(keywordQuery);
  if (exclusionQuery) parts.push(exclusionQuery);
  parts.push(sourceQuery);

  let fullQuery = parts.join(' ');

  // 9. Generate variants
  let variants = [];

  // Variant 1: Full, precise query
  variants.push(fullQuery);

  // Variant 2: Broader query (no exclusions, broader geography)
  let broadParts = parts.filter(p => !p.includes('-'));
  // Keep sources
  broadParts.push(sourceQuery);
  let broadQuery = broadParts.join(' ');
  variants.push(broadQuery);

  // Variant 3: Single-source focus (e.g., only Greenhouse)
  let singleSourceParts = parts.filter(p => !p.includes('site:'));
  let singleSourceQuery = singleSourceParts.join(' ') + ' site:greenhouse.io';
  variants.push(singleSourceQuery);

  // Variant 4: No source constraint (discovery mode) – useful for Google
  let discoveryParts = parts.filter(p => !p.includes('site:'));
  let discoveryQuery = discoveryParts.join(' ');
  variants.push(discoveryQuery);

  // 10. Return both the variants and the structured components for debugging
  return {
    variants: variants,
    structured: {
      roleQuery: roleQuery,
      geoQuery: geoQuery,
      remoteQuery: remoteQuery,
      exclusionQuery: exclusionQuery,
      keywordQuery: keywordQuery,
      sourceQuery: sourceQuery
    }
  };
}

/**
 * Test function – runs a sample query generation and logs the results.
 * Run this manually to verify everything works.
 */
function testQueryGen() {
  const params = {
    role: 'Operations Specialist',
    country: 'Nigeria',
    remote: 'Fully Remote',
    regions: 'Africa,EMEA',
    exclusions: ['US-only', 'Canada-only', 'UK-only'],
    keywords: 'excel automation',
    freshness: 7
  };

  const result = generateQueries(params);
  Logger.log('===== QUERY INTELLIGENCE TEST =====');
  Logger.log('Structured parts:');
  Logger.log('  Role: ' + result.structured.roleQuery);
  Logger.log('  Geo: ' + result.structured.geoQuery);
  Logger.log('  Remote: ' + result.structured.remoteQuery);
  Logger.log('  Exclusions: ' + result.structured.exclusionQuery);
  Logger.log('  Keywords: ' + result.structured.keywordQuery);
  Logger.log('  Sources: ' + result.structured.sourceQuery);
  Logger.log('\nGenerated Query Variants:');
  result.variants.forEach((q, i) => {
    Logger.log('  Variant ' + (i + 1) + ': ' + q);
  });
  Logger.log('===================================');

  // Also log to the AUDIT_LOG for traceability
  logEvent('QUERY_GEN_TEST', 'Generated ' + result.variants.length + ' variants for role: ' + params.role, 'INFO');

  return result;
}
```

svgsvg

**Important:** This script references `logEvent` from your `Logger.gs` – ensure `Logger.gs` is present and functional (it is, from Phase 1).
```

## Phase 4 – G2: Query Intelligence (Revised)

**Goal:** Convert a user’s professional profile or direct inputs into a structured **Query Plan** – a set of discovery strategies (Exact Role, Broad Role, Nigeria‑specific, ATS‑specific, Skills‑led, etc.) – without conflating geography, remote, or eligibility.  

**Output:** A new Apps Script module `QueryIntelligence.gs` that produces a JSON‑serializable plan, plus a Perchance generator that collects inputs and displays the plan (or clickable search links).  

**Exit Criteria:**  
- The function `buildQueryPlan(inputs)` returns a valid structured plan.  
- The plan contains at least 4 distinct strategies, each with a clear purpose and structured components.  
- Geography is never automatically expanded to “Worldwide” for remote.  
- Role synonyms are drawn from a controlled taxonomy (not naive word‑based).  
- A Perchance generator captures inputs and displays the plan to the user.  
- All tests (adversarial) pass (see attached test list).

```javascript
// ROLE TAXONOMY – controlled synonyms per role family
const ROLE_FAMILIES = {
  'Operations': [
    'Operations Specialist', 'Operations Associate', 'Operations Coordinator',
    'Business Operations', 'Operations Analyst', 'Operations Manager'
  ],
  'Product Operations': [
    'Product Operations Specialist', 'Product Operations Associate', 'Product Operations Manager'
  ],
  'Customer Operations': [
    'Customer Operations Specialist', 'Customer Operations Associate', 'Customer Operations Manager'
  ],
  'Support': [
    'Customer Support Specialist', 'Technical Support Specialist', 'Support Operations'
  ],
  'Research/Analysis': [
    'Research Analyst', 'Operations Analyst', 'Business Analyst', 'Data Analyst'
  ],
  'Automation/Systems': [
    'Automation Specialist', 'Workflow Specialist', 'Systems Operations', 'DevOps'
  ]
};

// GEOGRAPHY STRATEGIES – never automatically expand to Worldwide
const GEOGRAPHY_STRATEGIES = {
  'Nigeria': { type: 'country', label: 'Nigeria', terms: ['Nigeria'] },
  'Africa': { type: 'region', label: 'Africa', terms: ['Africa', 'EMEA'] },
  'EMEA': { type: 'region', label: 'EMEA', terms: ['EMEA', 'Europe', 'Middle East', 'Africa'] },
  'Worldwide': { type: 'global', label: 'Worldwide', terms: ['Worldwide', 'Global', 'Anywhere'] },
  'Remote (unspecified)': { type: 'remote', label: 'Remote – geography unspecified', terms: ['Remote'] }
};

// REMOTE TYPES
const REMOTE_TYPES = {
  'Fully Remote': 'Fully Remote',
  'Remote-First': 'Remote-First',
  'Hybrid': 'Hybrid',
  'On-site': 'On-site'
};
```

### Step 2 – Create `QueryIntelligence.gs`

Create a new script file named `QueryIntelligence.gs` and paste the following code:

```javascript
// QUERYINTELLIGENCE.GS – Builds a structured Query Plan from user inputs

/**
 * Main function: given user inputs, returns a Query Plan.
 * Inputs object should contain:
 *   - role: string (e.g., "Operations")
 *   - country: string (e.g., "Nigeria")
 *   - remotePreference: string (one of REMOTE_TYPES keys)
 *   - regions: array of strings (e.g., ["Africa", "EMEA"])
 *   - keywords: array of strings (e.g., ["Excel", "Automation"])
 *   - exclusions: array of strings (e.g., ["US-only", "Canada-only"])
 *   - freshnessDays: number (optional, default 7)
 */
function buildQueryPlan(inputs) {
  // 1. Validate inputs
  if (!inputs.role) throw new Error('Role is required');
  
  // 2. Determine role family and synonyms
  const roleFamily = findRoleFamily(inputs.role);
  const synonyms = roleFamily ? ROLE_FAMILIES[roleFamily] : [inputs.role];
  
  // 3. Geography strategies – do NOT add Worldwide automatically for remote
  const geographyStrategies = buildGeographyStrategies(inputs.country, inputs.regions || []);
  
  // 4. Remote strategy
  const remoteType = inputs.remotePreference || 'Fully Remote';
  
  // 5. Build the strategies array
  const strategies = [];
  
  // Strategy 1: Exact Role + Country (high precision)
  strategies.push({
    id: 'exact_country',
    purpose: 'High-precision search for the exact role in the specified country',
    role: inputs.role,
    synonyms: [inputs.role],
    geography: geographyStrategies.country,
    remote: remoteType,
    keywords: inputs.keywords || [],
    exclusions: inputs.exclusions || [],
    sources: ['google', 'greenhouse', 'lever', 'workable'], // can be refined later
    generatedQuery: buildQueryString(inputs.role, geographyStrategies.country.terms, remoteType, inputs.keywords, inputs.exclusions)
  });
  
  // Strategy 2: Role Synonyms + Country (increased recall)
  strategies.push({
    id: 'synonym_country',
    purpose: 'Search using role synonyms to catch variations',
    role: inputs.role,
    synonyms: synonyms.slice(0,5), // limit to avoid huge queries
    geography: geographyStrategies.country,
    remote: remoteType,
    keywords: inputs.keywords || [],
    exclusions: inputs.exclusions || [],
    sources: ['google', 'greenhouse', 'lever', 'workable'],
    generatedQuery: buildQueryString(synonyms.join(' OR '), geographyStrategies.country.terms, remoteType, inputs.keywords, inputs.exclusions)
  });
  
  // Strategy 3: Region (if specified) – e.g., Africa or EMEA
  if (geographyStrategies.region) {
    strategies.push({
      id: 'region',
      purpose: 'Search across a broader region when country-specific results are limited',
      role: inputs.role,
      synonyms: synonyms.slice(0,3),
      geography: geographyStrategies.region,
      remote: remoteType,
      keywords: inputs.keywords || [],
      exclusions: inputs.exclusions || [],
      sources: ['google', 'greenhouse', 'lever', 'workable'],
      generatedQuery: buildQueryString(synonyms.join(' OR '), geographyStrategies.region.terms, remoteType, inputs.keywords, inputs.exclusions)
    });
  }
  
  // Strategy 4: Global/Worldwide (only if user explicitly allows or no country/region)
  // We do NOT add this automatically; it must be requested.
  if (inputs.allowWorldwide === true) {
    strategies.push({
      id: 'worldwide',
      purpose: 'Global discovery for remote roles that are truly worldwide',
      role: inputs.role,
      synonyms: synonyms.slice(0,3),
      geography: { type: 'global', label: 'Worldwide', terms: ['Worldwide', 'Global', 'Anywhere'] },
      remote: remoteType,
      keywords: inputs.keywords || [],
      exclusions: inputs.exclusions || [],
      sources: ['google', 'greenhouse', 'lever', 'workable'],
      generatedQuery: buildQueryString(synonyms.join(' OR '), ['Worldwide', 'Global'], remoteType, inputs.keywords, inputs.exclusions)
    });
  }
  
  // Strategy 5: Skills-led (if keywords provided)
  if (inputs.keywords && inputs.keywords.length > 0) {
    strategies.push({
      id: 'skills_led',
      purpose: 'Search using skills rather than a specific job title',
      role: null,
      synonyms: [],
      geography: geographyStrategies.country,
      remote: remoteType,
      keywords: inputs.keywords,
      exclusions: inputs.exclusions || [],
      sources: ['google', 'greenhouse', 'lever', 'workable'],
      generatedQuery: buildQueryString(null, geographyStrategies.country.terms, remoteType, inputs.keywords, inputs.exclusions)
    });
  }
  
  // Strategy 6: Broad (maximum recall – no role, just keywords and geography)
  strategies.push({
    id: 'broad',
    purpose: 'Maximum recall for discovery when precise role returns few results',
    role: null,
    synonyms: [],
    geography: geographyStrategies.country,
    remote: remoteType,
    keywords: inputs.keywords || [],
    exclusions: inputs.exclusions || [],
    sources: ['google', 'greenhouse', 'lever', 'workable'],
    generatedQuery: buildQueryString(null, geographyStrategies.country.terms, remoteType, inputs.keywords, inputs.exclusions)
  });
  
  // Add source-specific strategies (e.g., Greenhouse)
  strategies.push({
    id: 'greenhouse',
    purpose: 'Direct search on Greenhouse ATS',
    role: inputs.role,
    synonyms: synonyms.slice(0,3),
    geography: geographyStrategies.country,
    remote: remoteType,
    keywords: inputs.keywords || [],
    exclusions: inputs.exclusions || [],
    sources: ['greenhouse'],
    generatedQuery: buildSourceQuery('greenhouse', inputs.role, geographyStrategies.country.terms, remoteType, inputs.keywords)
  });
  
  // Return the plan
  return {
    planId: 'PLAN-' + new Date().getTime(),
    generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    inputSummary: {
      role: inputs.role,
      country: inputs.country,
      remotePreference: remoteType,
      regions: inputs.regions || [],
      keywords: inputs.keywords || [],
      exclusions: inputs.exclusions || []
    },
    strategies: strategies,
    totalStrategies: strategies.length
  };
}

// Helper: find role family from a role string
function findRoleFamily(role) {
  const normalized = role.toLowerCase();
  for (const [family, synonyms] of Object.entries(ROLE_FAMILIES)) {
    if (synonyms.some(s => s.toLowerCase() === normalized)) return family;
    if (family.toLowerCase() === normalized) return family;
  }
  return null; // fallback to no family
}

// Helper: build geography strategies based on country and optional regions
function buildGeographyStrategies(country, regions) {
  const strategies = {};
  // Country strategy
  strategies.country = {
    type: 'country',
    label: country,
    terms: [country]
  };
  // Region strategy: if regions provided, use first region; else none
  if (regions && regions.length > 0) {
    const regionKey = regions[0]; // e.g., "Africa"
    // Map to known region terms
    const regionMap = {
      'Africa': { type: 'region', label: 'Africa', terms: ['Africa', 'EMEA'] },
      'EMEA': { type: 'region', label: 'EMEA', terms: ['EMEA', 'Europe', 'Middle East', 'Africa'] },
      'Asia': { type: 'region', label: 'Asia', terms: ['Asia'] },
      'Europe': { type: 'region', label: 'Europe', terms: ['Europe'] }
    };
    strategies.region = regionMap[regionKey] || { type: 'region', label: regionKey, terms: [regionKey] };
  }
  return strategies;
}

// Helper: build a query string from components
function buildQueryString(role, geographyTerms, remoteType, keywords, exclusions) {
  let parts = [];
  if (role) parts.push('(' + role + ')');
  if (geographyTerms && geographyTerms.length > 0) {
    parts.push('(' + geographyTerms.join(' OR ') + ')');
  }
  if (remoteType === 'Fully Remote' || remoteType === 'Remote-First') {
    parts.push('remote');
  }
  if (keywords && keywords.length > 0) {
    parts.push('(' + keywords.join(' OR ') + ')');
  }
  if (exclusions && exclusions.length > 0) {
    exclusions.forEach(term => {
      parts.push('-' + term);
    });
  }
  return parts.join(' ');
}

// Helper: build a source-specific query (e.g., site:greenhouse.io)
function buildSourceQuery(source, role, geographyTerms, remoteType, keywords) {
  let base = buildQueryString(role, geographyTerms, remoteType, keywords, []);
  if (source === 'greenhouse') return base + ' site:greenhouse.io';
  if (source === 'lever') return base + ' site:lever.co';
  if (source === 'workable') return base + ' site:workable.com';
  return base;
}
```

```javascript
function testQueryPlan() {

    role: 'Operations Specialist',

  // Assertions
  if (!plan.planId) throw new Error('No planId');
  if (plan.strategies.length < 4) throw new Error('Too few strategies');

  const hasWorldwide = plan.strategies.some(s => s.id === 'worldwide');

  Logger.log('Test passed: ' + plan.totalStrategies + ' strategies generated');
}
```

# ESE DIGITALS — PHASE 4 — G2 QUERY INTELLIGENCE  
## FINAL END-TO-END IMPLEMENTATION SPECIFICATION

**Status:** Final corrected G2 specification for implementation  
**Gate:** Phase 4 — G2 (Query Intelligence / 4A)  
**Purpose:** Convert a user's structured opportunity-search intent into a deterministic, auditable, machine-readable Query Plan that G3 can consume.  
**Implementation target:** Google Apps Script attached to `PDE_OS_MASTER`  
**Primary module:** `QueryEngine.gs`  
**Primary test module:** `QueryEngineTests.gs`  
**Interface position:** UI/front-end may collect the inputs, but Query Intelligence remains centralized in Apps Script.  
**G3 contract:** The output is JSON-serializable, versioned, deterministic in structure, and explicitly marked for G3 compatibility.  
**Frozen design principle:** This document fixes the remaining G2.1 QA gaps without reopening the prior architecture redesign.

> **IMPORTANT EXECUTION STATUS RULE**  
> This file is an implementation specification and execution guide. It does **not** claim that the user's Apps Script environment has already executed this code successfully. Completion must be established by running the supplied tests in the user's actual Apps Script project and retaining the resulting evidence.

---

# 1. CONTROLLING DECISIONS

The Phase 4 project manual establishes the Opportunity Intelligence Engine as the larger product context, with Query Intelligence as an early layer. The controlling rules for this gate are:

1. Query generation is an intelligence layer, not a collection of ad-hoc string substitutions.
2. Role resolution must use a controlled taxonomy.
3. Geography must remain explicit and must never be expanded to Worldwide merely because the user selected remote work.
4. `Remote` is a work-mode preference. It is not evidence of Worldwide eligibility and is not evidence of Nigerian eligibility.
5. User-country, target-country, preferred-region, and other geography concepts must not be silently conflated.
6. Raw user input must remain auditable while canonical values are used for deterministic logic.
7. Every generated strategy must conform to a common schema.
8. Strategy signatures must be unique within a Query Plan.
9. The plan must have a stable, versioned schema contract for G3.
10. ATS strategies are discovery strategies, not fabricated ATS records.
11. No private data, payment secret, API secret, credential, or internal CRM data belongs in the Query Plan.
12. Google search is a discovery mechanism. A search result is not proof that a job is live, eligible, or current.
13. No job application is automated by G2.
14. No strategy may silently invent geography, role titles, or eligibility.
15. If input is unresolved, the plan must fail closed for that dimension and record the unresolved condition instead of guessing.

These principles align with the master Phase 4 rules prohibiting fabrication and prohibiting the conflation of remote, worldwide, eligibility, freshness and evidence.

---

# 2. WHAT G2 IS — AND WHAT IT IS NOT

## 2.1 G2 IS

G2 is the controlled translation layer between user intent and discovery instructions.

The logical flow is:

```text
USER INTENT
    ↓
INPUT VALIDATION
    ↓
RAW-VALUE PRESERVATION
    ↓
CANONICAL NORMALIZATION
    ↓
ROLE RESOLUTION
    ↓
GEOGRAPHY RESOLUTION
    ↓
RETRIEVAL CONTEXT
    ↓
STRATEGY GENERATION
    ↓
STRATEGY-SCHEMA VALIDATION
    ↓
DUPLICATE-SIGNATURE VALIDATION
    ↓
PLAN VALIDATION
    ↓
VERSIONED QUERY PLAN
    ↓
G3 DISCOVERY
```

## 2.2 G2 IS NOT

G2 is **not**:

- a live job scraper;
- a job-verification engine;
- an eligibility adjudicator for individual jobs;
- a complete recommendation engine;
- an application automation system;
- a source of invented jobs;
- a promise that Google results are exhaustive;
- an assumption that `Fully Remote` means `Worldwide`;
- a reason to publish the private `PDE_OS_MASTER` workbook;
- a replacement for G3 structured ATS discovery.

The master Phase 4 manual explicitly places multi-source discovery, verification, evidence, eligibility and ranking after the query layer.

---

# 3. INPUT CONTRACT

The canonical `generateQueryPlan()` input object is designed to accept either arrays or comma-separated strings for fields where that is useful to the user interface.

## 3.1 Required / optional fields

```javascript
{
  role: string,
  country: string,
  targetCountries: string | string[],
  regions: string | string[],
  remotePreference: string,
  employmentType: string,
  keywords: string | string[],
  exclusions: string | string[],
  freshnessDays: number | string,
  allowWorldwide: boolean,
  preferredRegions: string | string[],
  workAuthorization: string,
  timezone: string,
  mode: string
}
```

## 3.2 Meaning of `country`

`country` means the user's stated base/home country for the profile context unless the front-end explicitly labels another meaning.

It is preserved as both:

- `userIntent.raw.country` — exact user-supplied value;
- `userIntent.canonical.country` — normalized canonical country, where resolvable.

## 3.3 Meaning of `targetCountries`

`targetCountries` means the countries in which the user wants to search for opportunities or which the user has explicitly identified as target hiring geographies.

This distinction prevents a future profile from accidentally using the user's own country as the only target opportunity geography.

If `targetCountries` is not supplied, G2 uses `country` as the initial exact-country discovery target **only because that is the conservative default for the current MVP profile model**. The plan records this in `geographyResolution.targetCountriesSource`.

That is a defaulting rule, not an eligibility claim.

## 3.4 Meaning of `regions`

`regions` are broader geographic preferences such as `Africa`, `EMEA`, `Europe`, `APAC`, etc.

Multiple regions are preserved and produce separate region strategies. They are not collapsed to the first item.

## 3.5 Meaning of `allowWorldwide`

`allowWorldwide === true` explicitly authorizes a Worldwide discovery strategy.

`allowWorldwide === false` means no Worldwide strategy is generated.

Remote preference alone can never set this flag to true.

## 3.6 Meaning of `freshnessDays`

`freshnessDays` is the user's preferred maximum posting age for downstream retrieval and filtering.

It is not treated as a fake Google search operator and is not silently inserted into search text as though Google guaranteed date semantics.

Valid range: **1–90 days**.

Out-of-range input causes an explicit validation error; it is not silently coerced.

---

# 4. G2 OUTPUT CONTRACT

The top-level output object is the canonical Query Plan.

```javascript
{
  schemaVersion: "2.1",
  taxonomyVersion: "1.0",
  geographyVersion: "1.0",
  planId: "PLAN-...",
  generatedAt: "ISO-8601 timestamp",
  generatedBy: "QueryEngine.gs",
  compatibleWith: ["G3"],
  status: "VALID" | "INVALID",
  executable: true | false,
  userIntent: {...},
  retrievalContext: {...},
  strategies: [...],
  totalStrategies: number,
  validation: {...}
}
```

## 4.1 The G3 contract

G3 must be able to consume the plan without reverse-engineering free text.

Every strategy therefore contains structured properties such as:

```javascript
{
  id,
  kind,
  purpose,
  sourceType,
  role,
  roleResolution,
  geography,
  remote,
  employmentType,
  keywords,
  exclusions,
  freshnessDays,
  retrieval,
  query,
  enabled,
  signature
}
```

The final Google query string exists as a convenience for Google discovery. It is not the canonical semantic representation.

---

# 5. CONTROLLED ROLE TAXONOMY

The role resolver must never use naive substring logic such as:

```javascript
if (role.toLowerCase().includes('operations')) { ... }
```

That approach causes false taxonomy expansion and makes results difficult to audit.

The controlled taxonomy below uses explicit tiers:

- `EXACT_TITLE` — canonical role title supplied or directly recognized;
- `RELATED_TITLE` — close controlled title in the same family;
- `ADJACENT_ROLE` — adjacent role that may legitimately capture relevant opportunities without pretending equivalence;
- `FAMILY` — the selected role family itself;
- `CUSTOM_ROLE` — user supplied role that is not in the controlled taxonomy;
- `EMPTY` — no usable role.

# 6. COUNTRY AND REGION MODELS

## 6.1 Country model

```javascript
  },
  Germany: {
    type: 'country',
    label: 'Germany',
    terms: ['Germany']
  }
};
```

## 6.2 Region model

The alias sets are deliberately non-overlapping at the normalized-key level so that country-like strings do not accidentally resolve to regions.

```javascript
const REGION_MODEL = {
  Africa: {
    type: 'region',
    label: 'Africa',
    terms: ['Africa']
  },
  EMEA: {
    type: 'region',
    label: 'EMEA',
    terms: ['EMEA', 'Europe Middle East Africa']
  },
  Europe: {
    type: 'region',
    label: 'Europe',
    terms: ['Europe']
  },
  Asia: {
    type: 'region',
    label: 'Asia',
    terms: ['Asia']
  },
  APAC: {
    type: 'region',
    label: 'APAC',
    terms: ['APAC', 'Asia Pacific', 'Asia-Pacific']
  },
  'North America': {
    type: 'region',
    label: 'North America',
    terms: ['North America']
  },
  LATAM: {
    type: 'region',
    label: 'LATAM',
    terms: ['LATAM', 'Latin America']
  },
  Worldwide: {
    type: 'global',
    label: 'Worldwide',
    terms: ['Worldwide', 'Global', 'Anywhere in the world']
  }
};
```

## 6.3 Remote model

```javascript
const REMOTE_TYPES = {
  'Fully Remote': 'Fully Remote',
  'Remote-First': 'Remote-First',
  Hybrid: 'Hybrid',
  'On-site': 'On-site'
};
```

Remote terminology is an independent dimension. It must not rewrite geography.

---

# 7. RAW-VALUE PRESERVATION AND NORMALIZATION

G2.1 QA requires a deliberate distinction between:

- the value the user actually typed;
- the canonical list used internally.

This means a scalar string must remain a scalar string in the raw record. It must not be silently converted to an array merely because the engine uses arrays internally.

## 7.1 Utility functions

```javascript
function cloneRawValue(value) {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.slice();
  if (value && typeof value === 'object') return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
  return value;
}

function splitRawToItems(value) {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    return value
      .map(v => String(v).trim())
      .filter(Boolean);
  }

  if (typeof value === 'string') {
    return value
      .split(',')
      .map(v => v.trim())
      .filter(Boolean);
  }

  if (value === null || value === undefined || value === '') return [];
  return [String(value).trim()].filter(Boolean);
}

function normalizeString(value) {
  return String(value === undefined || value === null ? '' : value)
    .trim()
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
}

function normalizeKey(value) {
  return normalizeString(value).toLowerCase();
}

function normalizeStringArray(value) {
  const items = splitRawToItems(value);
  const seen = new Set();
  const out = [];

  items.forEach(item => {
    const clean = normalizeString(item);
    const key = clean.toLowerCase();
    if (!clean || seen.has(key)) return;
    seen.add(key);
    out.push(clean);
  });

  return out;
}
```

## 7.2 Freshness normalization

```javascript
function normalizeFreshnessDays(value, defaultValue) {
  const fallback = defaultValue || 7;

  if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') {
    return {
      value: fallback,
      valid: true,
      reason: 'DEFAULTED'
    };
  }

  const n = Number(value);

  if (!Number.isFinite(n)) {
    return {
      value: null,
      valid: false,
      reason: 'FRESHNESS_NOT_NUMERIC'
    };
  }

  if (!Number.isInteger(n)) {
    return {
      value: null,
      valid: false,
      reason: 'FRESHNESS_NOT_INTEGER'
    };
  }

  if (n < 1 || n > 90) {
    return {
      value: null,
      valid: false,
      reason: 'FRESHNESS_OUT_OF_RANGE_1_TO_90'
    };
  }

  return {
    value: n,
    valid: true,
    reason: 'VALID'
  };
}
```

This specifically fixes the QA requirement that an invalid freshness value should produce a precise reason rather than silently defaulting.

---

# 8. ROLE RESOLUTION

Resolution order is frozen as:

```text
FAMILY
→ EXACT_TITLE
→ RELATED_TITLE
→ ADJACENT_ROLE
→ CUSTOM_ROLE
→ EMPTY
```

The resolver must return enough information for auditing and strategy construction.

```javascript
function resolveRole(rawRole) {
  const raw = cloneRawValue(rawRole);
  const normalized = normalizeString(rawRole);
  const key = normalizeKey(normalized);

  if (!key) {
    return {
      tier: 'EMPTY',
      family: null,
      canonicalRole: null,
      raw: raw,
      normalized: normalized,
      exactTitles: [],
      relatedTitles: [],
      adjacentRoles: [],
      reason: 'ROLE_EMPTY'
    };
  }

  const families = Object.keys(ROLE_TAXONOMY);

  // FAMILY first.
  for (const family of families) {
    if (normalizeKey(family) === key) {
      const tax = ROLE_TAXONOMY[family];
      return {
        tier: 'FAMILY',
        family: family,
        canonicalRole: family,
        raw: raw,
        normalized: normalized,
        exactTitles: tax.exact.slice(),
        relatedTitles: tax.related.slice(),
        adjacentRoles: tax.adjacent.slice(),
        reason: 'ROLE_MATCHED_FAMILY'
      };
    }
  }

  // EXACT_TITLE.
  for (const family of families) {
    const tax = ROLE_TAXONOMY[family];
    if (tax.exact.some(title => normalizeKey(title) === key)) {
      return {
        tier: 'EXACT_TITLE',
        family: family,
        canonicalRole: normalized,
        raw: raw,
        normalized: normalized,
        exactTitles: tax.exact.slice(),
        relatedTitles: tax.related.slice(),
        adjacentRoles: tax.adjacent.slice(),
        reason: 'ROLE_MATCHED_EXACT_TITLE'
      };
    }
  }

  // RELATED_TITLE.
  for (const family of families) {
    const tax = ROLE_TAXONOMY[family];
    if (tax.related.some(title => normalizeKey(title) === key)) {
      return {
        tier: 'RELATED_TITLE',
        family: family,
        canonicalRole: normalized,
        raw: raw,
        normalized: normalized,
        exactTitles: tax.exact.slice(),
        relatedTitles: tax.related.slice(),
        adjacentRoles: tax.adjacent.slice(),
        reason: 'ROLE_MATCHED_RELATED_TITLE'
      };
    }
  }

  // ADJACENT_ROLE.
  for (const family of families) {
    const tax = ROLE_TAXONOMY[family];
    if (tax.adjacent.some(title => normalizeKey(title) === key)) {
      return {
        tier: 'ADJACENT_ROLE',
        family: family,
        canonicalRole: normalized,
        raw: raw,
        normalized: normalized,
        exactTitles: tax.exact.slice(),
        relatedTitles: tax.related.slice(),
        adjacentRoles: tax.adjacent.slice(),
        reason: 'ROLE_MATCHED_ADJACENT_ROLE'
      };
    }
  }

  // CUSTOM_ROLE.
  return {
    tier: 'CUSTOM_ROLE',
    family: null,
    canonicalRole: normalized,
    raw: raw,
    normalized: normalized,
    exactTitles: [normalized],
    relatedTitles: [],
    adjacentRoles: [],
    reason: 'ROLE_TREATED_AS_CUSTOM_ROLE'
  };
}
```

## 8.1 Role semantics

`FAMILY` does not mean every title is equivalent. It means the user selected a family and the engine may use the controlled exact/related/adjacent tiers for separate discovery purposes.

`EXACT_TITLE` does not authorize the engine to invent related roles outside the family.

`RELATED_TITLE` is not silently relabeled as exact.

`ADJACENT_ROLE` is optional recall support and must remain visibly distinct.

`CUSTOM_ROLE` is preserved as entered and is not matched to a family unless taxonomy is explicitly updated.

---

# 9. COUNTRY AND REGION RESOLUTION

## 9.1 Country normalization

```javascript
function normalizeCountry(rawCountry) {
  const raw = cloneRawValue(rawCountry);
  const text = normalizeString(rawCountry);
  const key = normalizeKey(text);

  if (!key) {
    return {
      raw: raw,
      normalized: text,
      canonical: null,
      resolved: false,
      reason: 'COUNTRY_EMPTY'
    };
  }

  for (const [canonical, model] of Object.entries(COUNTRY_MODEL)) {
    const aliases = [canonical].concat(model.terms || []);
    if (aliases.some(term => normalizeKey(term) === key)) {
      return {
        raw: raw,
        normalized: text,
        canonical: canonical,
        resolved: true,
        reason: 'COUNTRY_RESOLVED'
      };
    }
  }

  return {
    raw: raw,
    normalized: text,
    canonical: null,
    resolved: false,
    reason: 'COUNTRY_UNRESOLVED'
  };
}
```

## 9.2 Region normalization

```javascript
function normalizeRegion(rawRegion) {
  const raw = cloneRawValue(rawRegion);
  const text = normalizeString(rawRegion);
  const key = normalizeKey(text);

  if (!key) {
    return {
      raw: raw,
      normalized: text,
      canonical: null,
      resolved: false,
      reason: 'REGION_EMPTY'
    };
  }

  for (const [canonical, model] of Object.entries(REGION_MODEL)) {
    const aliases = [canonical].concat(model.terms || []);
    if (aliases.some(term => normalizeKey(term) === key)) {
      return {
        raw: raw,
        normalized: text,
        canonical: canonical,
        resolved: true,
        reason: 'REGION_RESOLVED'
      };
    }
  }

  return {
    raw: raw,
    normalized: text,
    canonical: null,
    resolved: false,
    reason: 'REGION_UNRESOLVED'
  };
}
```

## 9.3 Multiple regions

All region inputs are resolved independently.

Example:

```javascript
regions: ['Africa', 'EMEA', 'APAC']
```

must produce three region resolutions and three separate region strategies, subject to deterministic de-duplication.

The engine must **not** keep only the first region.

## 9.4 Unresolved geography

Unresolved geography is never converted into `Worldwide` as a fallback.

Instead:

```javascript
{
  raw: 'Some Custom Region',
  canonical: null,
  resolved: false,
  reason: 'REGION_UNRESOLVED'
}
```

is retained in `geographyResolution.unresolvedRegions` and a validation warning is emitted.

If there is no usable country or region, the engine may still create a discovery plan using explicitly requested global or remote semantics, but it must label the plan accordingly and must not claim country eligibility.

---

# 10. GEOGRAPHY RESOLUTION MODEL

The plan contains both the user's profile geography and the target discovery geography.

Example:

```javascript
{
  userCountry: {
    raw: 'Nigeria',
    canonical: 'Nigeria',
    resolved: true
  },
  targetCountries: {
    source: 'EXPLICIT',
    raw: ['Nigeria'],
    canonical: ['Nigeria'],
    unresolved: []
  },
  regions: {
    raw: ['Africa', 'EMEA'],
    canonical: ['Africa', 'EMEA'],
    unresolved: []
  },
  allowWorldwide: false,
  targetCountriesSource: 'EXPLICIT'
}
```

When `targetCountries` is omitted:

```javascript
{
  targetCountriesSource: 'DEFAULTED_FROM_USER_COUNTRY'
}
```

This distinction is important because a future user may live in Nigeria but intentionally search for Europe or North America opportunities.

---

# 11. RETRIEVAL CONTEXT

The strategy generator should not force G3 to infer every downstream retrieval requirement from free text.

The final plan includes:

```javascript
retrievalContext: {
  requestedFreshnessDays,
  sourceClasses,
  atsEndpointMode,
  googleDiscoveryAllowed,
  canonicalIdAllowedInGoogleQuery,
  verificationRequiredDownstream,
  eligibilityRequiredDownstream,
  applicationAutomation: 'PROHIBITED'
}
```

## 11.1 Frozen ATS mode

```javascript
const ATS_ENDPOINT_MODE = 'PUBLIC_JOB_POSTINGS_API';
```

G2 does not pretend to call those APIs. It tells G3 that ATS strategies are intended for public job-posting endpoints.

## 11.2 Source classes

The plan may reference:

- `GOOGLE_SEARCH`
- `GREENHOUSE`
- `LEVER`
- `ASHBY`

The earlier G2.1 QA correction explicitly restored Ashby to the structured source strategy set.

## 11.3 Google query identifier rule

Canonical internal identifiers such as `PLAN-*`, `ROLE-*`, or database IDs must not be inserted into Google queries.

A Google query should contain discoverable terms, not private or internal IDs.

---

# 12. GOOGLE QUERY CONSTRUCTION

The query builder must treat query text as a rendered view over structured intent.

```javascript
function quoteIfNeeded(value) {
  const text = normalizeString(value);
  if (!text) return '';
  if (/^".*"$/.test(text)) return text;
  if (/\s/.test(text)) return '"' + text.replace(/"/g, '') + '"';
  return text;
}

function buildRoleClause(roleTerms) {
  const terms = normalizeStringArray(roleTerms);
  if (!terms.length) return '';
  if (terms.length === 1) return quoteIfNeeded(terms[0]);
  return '(' + terms.map(quoteIfNeeded).join(' OR ') + ')';
}

function buildGeographyClause(geographyTerms) {
  const terms = normalizeStringArray(geographyTerms);
  if (!terms.length) return '';
  if (terms.length === 1) return quoteIfNeeded(terms[0]);
  return '(' + terms.map(quoteIfNeeded).join(' OR ') + ')';
}

function buildRemoteClause(remotePreference) {
  const remote = normalizeString(remotePreference);

  if (remote === 'Fully Remote') {
    return '(remote OR "work from anywhere" OR "work remotely")';
  }

  if (remote === 'Remote-First') {
    return '(remote-first OR remote)';
  }

  if (remote === 'Hybrid') {
    return '(hybrid OR remote)';
  }

  if (remote === 'On-site') {
    return '(on-site OR onsite)';
  }

  return '';
}

function buildExclusionClause(exclusions) {
  const terms = normalizeStringArray(exclusions);
  if (!terms.length) return '';

  return terms
    .map(term => '-' + quoteIfNeeded(term))
    .join(' ');
}

function buildKeywordClause(keywords) {
  const terms = normalizeStringArray(keywords);
  if (!terms.length) return '';
  if (terms.length === 1) return quoteIfNeeded(terms[0]);
  return '(' + terms.map(quoteIfNeeded).join(' OR ') + ')';
}

function buildSiteClause(domains) {
  const terms = normalizeStringArray(domains);
  if (!terms.length) return '';
  if (terms.length === 1) return 'site:' + terms[0];
  return '(' + terms.map(d => 'site:' + d).join(' OR ') + ')';
}

function buildGoogleQuery(options) {
  const parts = [];

  const roleClause = buildRoleClause(options.roleTerms || []);
  const geoClause = buildGeographyClause(options.geographyTerms || []);
  const remoteClause = buildRemoteClause(options.remotePreference || '');
  const keywordClause = buildKeywordClause(options.keywords || []);
  const exclusionClause = buildExclusionClause(options.exclusions || []);
  const siteClause = buildSiteClause(options.siteDomains || []);

  if (roleClause) parts.push(roleClause);
  if (geoClause) parts.push(geoClause);
  if (remoteClause) parts.push(remoteClause);
  if (keywordClause) parts.push(keywordClause);
  if (exclusionClause) parts.push(exclusionClause);
  if (siteClause) parts.push(siteClause);

  return parts.join(' ').trim();
}
```

## 12.1 Important syntax rule

Correct:

```text
site:greenhouse.io
site:lever.co
site:ashbyhq.com
```

Incorrect:

```text
site:://greenhouse.io
site://lever.co
```

The engine must contain a regression test for malformed `site:` syntax.

---

# 13. SOURCE STRATEGIES

The final G2 plan uses explicit strategy IDs and exact composition.

## 13.1 Strategy types

### Strategy A — `EXACT_ROLE_COUNTRY`

High precision. Exact canonical/current title plus a target country.

### Strategy B — `EXACT_ROLE_REGION`

One strategy per resolved target region.

### Strategy C — `FAMILY_COUNTRY`

Controlled family expansion against country when family resolution provides additional titles.

### Strategy D — `SKILLS_LED`

Skills-led discovery when useful keywords are supplied.

### Strategy E — `ATS_API`

One structured ATS strategy per supported ATS source.

### Strategy F — `UNRESOLVED_DISCOVERY`

Fail-safe discovery path when there is insufficient resolved geography/role information but a discoverable input remains.

The exact strategy count is deterministic for a given input.

---

# 14. STRATEGY SCHEMA

Every strategy must pass the same invariant schema.

```javascript
function buildStrategyBase(options) {
  return {
    id: options.id,
    kind: options.kind,
    purpose: options.purpose,
    sourceType: options.sourceType,
    role: options.role,
    roleResolution: options.roleResolution,
    geography: options.geography,
    remote: options.remote,
    employmentType: options.employmentType,
    keywords: options.keywords,
    exclusions: options.exclusions,
    freshnessDays: options.freshnessDays,
    retrieval: options.retrieval,
    query: options.query,
    enabled: options.enabled !== false,
    signature: options.signature
  };
}
```

## 14.1 Strategy schema invariant

The following keys are mandatory for **every** strategy:

```text
id
kind
purpose
sourceType
role
roleResolution
geography
remote
employmentType
keywords
exclusions
freshnessDays
retrieval
query
enabled
signature
```

The test suite must fail if any required key is missing.

---

# 15. STRATEGY SIGNATURES

Duplicate strategies are not acceptable even if their IDs differ.

A strategy signature is a stable normalized identity built from semantic components.

```javascript
function makeStrategySignature(parts) {
  return [
    parts.kind || '',
    parts.sourceType || '',
    normalizeString(parts.role || ''),
    JSON.stringify(normalizeStringArray(parts.roleTerms || [])),
    JSON.stringify(normalizeStringArray(parts.geographyTerms || [])),
    normalizeString(parts.remote || ''),
    normalizeString(parts.employmentType || ''),
    JSON.stringify(normalizeStringArray(parts.keywords || [])),
    JSON.stringify(normalizeStringArray(parts.exclusions || [])),
    String(parts.freshnessDays || '')
  ].join('|').toLowerCase();
}
```

The final plan must contain no duplicate `signature` values.

This specifically implements the G2.1 QA requirement that duplicate-strategy signatures fail rather than being silently tolerated.

---

Supported ATS sources for the frozen G2/G3 contract:

```javascript
const ATS_SOURCES = [
```

```javascript
function cloneRawValue(value) {

  if (value && typeof value === 'object') return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));

function splitRawToItems(value) {

}

    .trim()

    if (!clean || seen.has(key)) return;
    seen.add(key);
    out.push(clean);
  });
  return out;
}

    return { value: fallback, valid: true, reason: 'DEFAULTED' };
```
