NIGERIAN RAILWAY CORPORATION
NRC Chalet Asset Commercialisation, Hospitality Development & Revenue Optimisation Master Blueprint
Business case framework, operating model, refurbishment, governance, digital architecture and implementation toolkit
Location: Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos | Units: 12
Prepared: 3 September 2026 | Working Draft for Management Consideration
Document ID: NRC-COMP-CHAL-001 | Version 1.0
Document Control
Executive Summary
This blueprint proposes that NRC assess, pilot and, where justified, scale a professionally managed serviced-accommodation proposition using the 12 existing chalet units at Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos. The objective is not to create an informal rental arrangement, but to establish a governed public-asset commercialisation model that can generate sustainable revenue, preserve the underlying asset, improve utilisation and create a transparent operating and financial control environment.
The supplied architectural description suggests the units can be positioned commercially as one-bedroom serviced bungalows/suites: a distinct bedroom with ensuite, an intermediate lobby with visitor WC/wardrobe, a living/dining area, a service lobby and a compact kitchen. The final product standard remains subject to physical inspection and actual drawings/photographs.
Figure 1. Chalet photograph placeholder - replace with inspection photographs.
1. Strategic Opportunity
The opportunity is to convert under-utilised NRC accommodation assets into professionally managed serviced accommodation without compromising public-asset governance. NRC’s statutory framework contemplates provision of hotels, hostels and other accommodation and amenities; NRC’s public property-management ecosystem also describes commercialisable land and building assets and revenue optimisation. The precise authority and operating route for these 12 units must nevertheless be confirmed in writing for the specific asset.
The project should therefore be positioned as an asset optimisation initiative, not as a request to “rent out the chalets”. The recommended decision is a controlled pilot leading to scale only if legal, financial, operational and customer metrics are met.
2. Project Objectives
Generate additional lawful and sustainable revenue for NRC.
Improve utilisation and condition of existing accommodation assets.
Establish a premium, walk-in, one-bedroom serviced-accommodation product.
Create transparent booking, payment, accounting and asset-control processes.
Reduce revenue leakage, asset deterioration and unmanaged occupancy.
Develop a repeatable model that can be applied to other suitable NRC properties.
3. Non-Goals
The programme does not authorise disposal, sale, lease, concession or transfer of NRC property. Those are separate legal/commercial decisions.
The programme does not assume that external hospitality operation is automatically permissible.
The financial model does not assert market rates or guaranteed profitability. All initial figures are illustrative planning assumptions to be replaced by survey and market evidence.
4. Legal, Regulatory and Institutional Framework
The legal workstream should establish a written Authority and Commercialisation Matrix for this exact property. The matrix should cover the NRC Act; current NRC conditions/instruments; property and subsidiary arrangements; Public Procurement Act/BPP requirements; financial regulations; applicable Lagos planning/building-control requirements; hospitality/tourism registration; health, fire, environmental, signage and tax obligations; data protection; payment/financial controls; and any Ministry or Board approvals required.
5. Asset Discovery and Physical Condition
Undertake a unit-by-unit technical survey. Record room sizes, roof, walls, ceilings, floors, windows, doors, plumbing, electrical systems, HVAC, water storage, drainage, security, accessibility, parking, external works, furniture and appliances. Assign each unit a condition grade A-E and a scope of refurbishment.
6. Proposed Product Definition
Position the units as NRC Executive Serviced Suites / Luxury One-Bedroom Serviced Bungalows. The product standard should include a private bedroom and ensuite, visitor WC, living/dining zone, fully equipped kitchen, quality sleep system, reliable power/water, internet, security and housekeeping. All detailed furniture and specifications remain placeholders pending inspection.
7. Customer Segments
Prioritise corporate travellers, railway-related visitors, approved government/institutional guests, project teams, consultants, transit customers and general short-stay customers where permitted. Validate demand through market research rather than assumptions.
8. Commercial Models to Evaluate
Model A: NRC direct operation. Model B: professional management contract. Model C: revenue-share arrangement. Model D: concession/other commercial structure. Score each for legal viability, financial return, NRC control, capital requirement, operating risk, procurement complexity and scalability.
9. Preliminary Operating Preference
Subject to legal and procurement confirmation, the preferred design hypothesis is NRC retaining ownership/control while using appropriate professional hospitality capability through an authorised operating arrangement. This is a preliminary design hypothesis, not a final award recommendation.
10. Refurbishment Strategy
Do not renovate all 12 units before proving the commercial model. Use a 3-5 unit pilot or other management-approved cohort after technical and financial analysis. Refurbish to one consistent brand standard, then scale.
11. Walk-In Readiness Standard
Guest should arrive with clothing/personal effects rather than bedding, kitchen equipment or household basics. Provide linen, toiletries, cookware, appliances, Wi-Fi, TV, power/water arrangements, cleaning and core guest supplies.
12. Property Layout Interpretation
The conceptual flow is: Front entry -> living/dining -> service lobby -> kitchen; bedroom side -> sleeping suite/ensuite; bedroom/living transition -> visitor WC + wardrobe/luggage zone. The supplied “linear/corridor” description should be checked against actual photographs and measured drawings before final design.
13. Hospitality Operating Model
Define reservation, pre-arrival, check-in, guest service, housekeeping, maintenance, inspection, checkout, inventory reconciliation, complaint handling, incident management and post-stay feedback. Every function must have an owner and SLA.
14. Revenue Management
Use approved tariffs, corporate rates, long-stay packages and controlled dynamic pricing where appropriate. All rate overrides and discounts should be authorised, logged and reportable.
15. Financial Model
Calculate occupancy, average daily rate, revenue per available unit, room revenue, ancillary revenue, direct costs, fixed operating costs, net operating income, capital expenditure, break-even occupancy, payback, NPV, IRR and sensitivity. Replace illustrative assumptions with survey/quote evidence before approval.
16. Digital Platform
Deploy a lightweight property/booking system with availability, booking, payment reference, invoices, housekeeping status, maintenance, guest records, inventory, revenue reports and management dashboards. Design for API integration, auditability, MFA/RBAC and low-bandwidth access.
17. Financial Controls
Every booking must link to an invoice/payment record and ultimately to bank/accounting reconciliation. Prevent unauthorised free rooms, undocumented discounts, unapproved refunds, occupancy without payment and manual rate changes.
18. Asset Controls
Assign asset IDs to televisions, ACs, refrigerators, microwaves, furniture and other significant equipment. Record issue, condition, maintenance and loss/damage at unit level.
19. Governance
Establish an Executive Steering Committee, Project Manager/PMO, Commercial Lead, Property/Engineering Lead, Finance Lead, Legal Lead, Procurement Lead, ICT Lead, Internal Audit/Risk representative and Operations Lead.
20. Procurement
Determine whether the required route is procurement of works, goods, services, management services, lease/licence/concession or another lawful route. Obtain Procurement and Legal sign-off before approaching the market. Use BPP-compliant documents and an auditable evaluation model.
21. Lagos Approvals
Renovation/alteration and any change of use should be screened with the relevant Lagos planning/building authorities. Lagos State’s official sources state that planning permits are required for development and that building-control processes apply to renovation and conversion; the precise route depends on the scope and existing approvals.
22. Health, Safety, Fire and Environment
Complete fire/life-safety assessment, emergency egress review, electrical safety, water quality, sanitation, pest control, waste management and occupational safety review. No unit should be opened until it passes the approved readiness checklist.
23. Guest Data and Privacy
Collect only necessary guest information. Define purpose, access, retention, privacy notice, processor relationships, security and incident response. Complete a DPIA before the platform goes live.
24. Risk Management
Track legal/property, demand, capex, utilities, service quality, procurement, revenue leakage, fraud, cybersecurity, privacy, reputation and vendor-dependency risks. Each risk gets an owner, likelihood, impact and mitigation.
25. Pilot Design
Pilot 3-5 representative units; measure occupancy, ADR, guest satisfaction, cost per occupied night, utilities, maintenance and net revenue for at least a management-approved period. Scale only if stage-gate metrics are achieved.
26. Implementation Roadmap
Stage 0 mandate -> Stage 1 legal/asset discovery -> Stage 2 market study -> Stage 3 business case -> Stage 4 design/QS/procurement -> Stage 5 refurbishment -> Stage 6 technology -> Stage 7 commissioning -> Stage 8 pilot -> Stage 9 scale -> Stage 10 benefits realisation.
27. Target Operating Process
Asset/legal readiness
Establishment of tariff/product
Pre-opening inspection
Inventory and unit readiness
Bookings
Payment verification
Check-in
Housekeeping/service
Maintenance/incident handling
Checkout and inventory check
Revenue reconciliation
Guest feedback
Management reporting
Audit and improvement
28. Proposed KPI Framework
29. Stage-Gate Approval Framework
30. Initial Work Breakdown Structure
31. Key Deliverables Checklist
Approved project charter
Legal opinion / authority matrix
Asset register and condition survey
Measured drawings and refurbishment design
Bill of quantities / cost plan
Market and competitor survey
Tariff framework
Three-scenario financial model
Operating manual/SOPs
Staffing and training plan
Procurement strategy/TOR/RFP
Technology requirements and data model
Privacy/DPIA package
Security assessment
Pilot plan
Management approval paper
Benefits-realisation plan

NIGERIAN RAILWAY CORPORATION
Executive Proposal to Management
Pilot Commercialisation of 12 NRC Chalet Units, Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos
Location: Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos | Units: 12
Prepared: 3 September 2026 | Working Draft for Management Consideration
Document ID: NRC-COMP-CHAL-002 | Version 1.0
Proposed Decision
Management is requested to approve the development and evaluation of a controlled pilot to rehabilitate and commercially operate selected units within the 12-unit NRC chalet facility at Ebute Metta, subject to completion of legal, property, procurement, technical, market and financial due diligence.
Management Rationale
NRC has an existing accommodation asset with a plausible serviced-accommodation use case.
The 12-unit scale is sufficiently small to test the commercial model without committing to an uncontrolled full-scale rollout.
The operating concept can create a transparent revenue stream while improving asset condition and utilisation.
The proposal can be implemented through an approved NRC operating structure without presuming that the proponent personally receives the asset or management rights.
Why Now
The project sits at the intersection of asset utilisation, revenue optimisation, hospitality service and digital financial controls. NRC’s public-facing Finance & Accounts, Internal Audit, Operations & Commercial and RPMCL materials already identify revenue, asset safeguarding, market survey and property commercialisation functions that can anchor the initiative. See Source Register.
Recommended Pilot
High-Level Financial Logic
The accompanying financial workbook uses illustrative planning assumptions only. It calculates unit nights, room revenue, ancillary revenue, operating costs, net operating revenue, break-even and payback. No planning assumption should be mistaken for a market quote or guaranteed return. Final investment recommendation should use independent market survey, QS pricing and vendor quotations.
Requested Management Authorisations
Permit formal feasibility/discovery work for the 12 units.
Nominate an executive sponsor and cross-functional project team.
Authorise site inspection, asset register and technical condition survey.
Direct Legal/Property/RPMCL (as appropriate) to confirm control, permissible commercial structure and approvals.
Direct Finance/Procurement/Internal Audit to design the revenue, procurement and control framework.
Authorise preparation of a 3-5 unit pilot business case with evidence-backed CAPEX/OPEX.
Require a return-to-Management stage-gate paper before any operator appointment or major capital commitment.
Important Governance Position

NIGERIAN RAILWAY CORPORATION
NRC Chalet Commercialisation Business Case
Feasibility framework, scenario economics, investment gates and commercial evaluation
Location: Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos | Units: 12
Prepared: 3 September 2026 | Working Draft for Management Consideration
Document ID: NRC-COMP-CHAL-003 | Version 1.0
1. Purpose
This business case establishes the analytical framework for deciding whether and how the 12-unit chalet facility should be renovated and commercialised. It intentionally separates hard facts from planning assumptions.
2. Known Facts at This Stage
3. Illustrative Planning Assumptions
4. Scenario Outputs (Illustrative)
Illustrative outputs are mathematical results from the stated assumptions; they are not market forecasts.
5. Illustrative CAPEX and Payback Framework
6. Required Market Work
Identify at least 10-15 directly comparable hotels/serviced apartments within the catchment area.
Record advertised rate by room category, occupancy proxy, amenities, power/water reliability, parking, security and booking-channel presence.
Run a corporate demand survey focused on railway-linked organisations, contractors, project firms and other likely customers.
Validate weekday/weekend demand and seasonal effects.
Test willingness to pay before finalising the room-rate ladder.
7. Break-Even
Break-even occupancy should be calculated in the spreadsheet as fixed costs divided by contribution margin per available night. Management should review the result under different ADR and variable-cost assumptions.
8. Sensitivity
9. Investment Recommendation Logic
Proceed only if legal authority is confirmed.
Proceed only if asset condition and renovation scope are technically feasible.
Proceed only if the market supports a viable rate/occupancy combination.
Proceed only if the selected commercial model produces acceptable risk-adjusted net revenue.
Proceed only with a transparent procurement/contract route and financial controls.
Use pilot evidence before scaling all 12 units.

Hospitality Operations Manual & Standard Operating Procedures

Operating Policy
The facility shall operate as a professionally managed serviced-accommodation property with standardised guest service, financial control, asset protection and safety processes. No room may be sold or occupied until it is “Ready” under the room-readiness checklist.
SOP-01 Reservation
Receive booking
Verify dates and unit availability
Apply approved tariff
Issue booking reference
Confirm payment or approved billing
Notify housekeeping
Record guest data only as necessary
SOP-02 Pre-Arrival
Check booking/payment
Prepare unit
Check power/water/internet
Confirm linen/toiletries
Inspect kitchen equipment
Set room status to READY
SOP-03 Check-In
Verify booking reference and approved guest identity process
Issue access
Explain house rules and emergency information
Record check-in time
Escalate exceptions
SOP-04 Housekeeping
Clean bedroom/ensuite/lobby/living/kitchen
Change linen
Restock consumables
Inspect appliances
Record defects
Supervisor sign-off
SOP-05 Maintenance
Log fault
Classify severity
Assign technician
Record start/finish
Verify repair
Return unit to READY or MAINTENANCE
SOP-06 Checkout
Confirm checkout
Inspect unit
Reconcile inventory
Record damage/defects
Close stay
Trigger room cleaning
Reconcile billing
SOP-07 Revenue Reconciliation
Match booking to invoice/payment
Confirm bank/accounting evidence
Investigate unmatched items
Escalate variances
Daily sign-off
SOP-08 Guest Complaint
Acknowledge
Categorise
Assign owner
Resolve
Record cause
Close with guest feedback
SOP-09 Incident & Emergency
Protect life first
Notify appropriate emergency/security personnel
Record incident
Preserve evidence
Notify management
Complete corrective action
SOP-10 Inventory
Maintain asset register
Monthly spot checks
Checkout inspections
Loss/damage reporting
Replacement approval
Room Status Codes
Housekeeping Readiness Checklist
Service Standards
Staffing Model - Initial Hypothesis
Guest House Rules - Draft
No unauthorised subletting or transfer of booking.
No alteration or removal of NRC property.
Guests must comply with security, fire and emergency rules.
Smoking, events, commercial filming, pets and other controlled activities should be governed by an approved policy.
Damage and loss handling shall follow a published, non-arbitrary policy.

1. Background
NRC intends to evaluate the commercial utilisation of 12 accommodation units at Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos. This TOR provides a procurement-ready framework; it is not itself a procurement advertisement and must be adjusted to the procurement route approved by NRC Procurement and Legal.
2. Possible Scope Packages
3. Minimum Bidder Requirements
Demonstrable hospitality/property-management experience relevant to serviced accommodation.
Evidence of financial capacity and valid corporate/tax registrations as applicable.
Named key personnel and professional qualifications where required.
Health, safety, quality and cybersecurity capabilities appropriate to scope.
Ability to provide transparent reporting, reconciliations and audit access.
Ability to provide local after-sales/support capability for digital systems where applicable.
4. Mandatory Deliverables
Detailed mobilisation plan
Operating procedures
Staffing and training plan
Tariff/revenue-management proposal
Digital booking/PMS configuration
Financial reporting and reconciliation procedures
Asset inventory and maintenance plan
Guest service standards
Monthly management dashboard
Risk and incident reporting
Business continuity and disaster recovery plan
Data protection/security documentation
Exit/transition plan
5. Evaluation Framework
Weights are illustrative and must be aligned to the approved procurement method and solicitation documents.
6. Contract Controls
NRC ownership/control of data and records.
Audit rights over booking, payment, staffing, inventory and vendor charges.
Defined performance KPIs and service credits/remedies where appropriate.
No unauthorised sub-contracting.
Clear treatment of guest data and processors.
Defined termination, transition and handover.
Insurance and indemnity requirements as determined by Legal/Procurement.
Asset custody and damage/loss rules.
7. Payment Model Options
Fixed management fee
Fee plus performance component
Revenue share
Cost-plus only where justified and tightly controlled
Other lawful structure approved after financial/legal review

Route-to-market note
Approved TOR/RFP
Bid evaluation committee and conflict declarations
Bid clarification log
Evaluation report
Negotiation/BAFO documentation where applicable

[TABLE 3]
ID | Risk | Rating | Mitigation
R01 | Unclear legal authority/commercial structure | Critical | Early legal/property opinion; no commitment until gate
R02 | Asset ownership/control ambiguity | Critical | Asset register and written control determination
R03 | Renovation cost overrun | High | Independent QS + contingency + stage-gated works
R04 | Weak market demand | High | Market survey + 3-5 unit pilot
R05 | Power cost erodes margin | High | Energy audit + hybrid options + metering
R06 | Revenue leakage | Critical | Digital booking/payment + daily reconciliation
R07 | Poor service quality | High | SOPs + training + QA + guest feedback
R08 | Data breach | High | MFA/RBAC/encryption/DPIA/testing
R09 | Procurement challenge | Critical | Early Procurement/Legal engagement
R10 | Property/permit non-compliance | High | Planning/building/tourism/HSE checklist
R11 | Vendor lock-in | Medium/High | Data portability + exit plan + API
R12 | Asset theft/damage | High | Inventory + inspection + security controls

Asset loss | Unit inventory/checkout check | Monthly asset spot check | Operations/Property

[SLIDE 1]
NRC Chalet Asset Commercialisation
12 units | Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos
Management concept deck
Serviced accommodation + asset optimisation + revenue controls
Working draft - 3 September 2026
1

[SLIDE 2]
The opportunity
Commercial rationale
Convert an under-utilised accommodation asset into a governed revenue-generating hospitality product
Preserve the underlying NRC asset while improving utilisation
Start with a controlled pilot; scale only on evidence
2

[SLIDE 3]
What we know / what remains to verify
Facts, gaps and evidence status
Known: 12 units; location; renovation required
To verify: measured drawings, exact condition, utilities, permits, furniture, equipment, asset-control position
Photographs in this deck are placeholders
3

[SLIDE 4]
Proposed commercial product
Walk-in executive serviced accommodation
Executive serviced one-bedroom bungalow / suite
Private bedroom + ensuite
Visitor WC and wardrobe/luggage transition zone
Living/dining + fully equipped kitchen
Walk-in ready: guest brings personal effects, not household setup
4

[SLIDE 5]
Conceptual guest journey
Customer lifecycle
Discover → Book → Pay → Confirm → Arrive → Check-in → Stay → Service → Checkout → Feedback
Digital booking/payment controls support the customer journey
5

[SLIDE 6]
Four operating models
Commercial structures to evaluate
A. NRC direct operation
B. Professional management contract
C. Revenue-share arrangement
D. Concession/other structure
Select only after legal, procurement and financial evaluation
6

[SLIDE 7]
Recommended design hypothesis
Preliminary operating recommendation
NRC retains ownership/control
Professional hospitality capability may be engaged through an authorised route
No informal allocation or unmanaged private operation
Pilot 3-5 units before full rollout
7

[SLIDE 8]
Financial logic
Illustrative economics
Revenue = occupied nights × ADR + ancillary revenue
Key metrics: occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, cost/occupied night, NOI, break-even, payback
Initial workbook assumptions are illustrative and replaceable
8

[SLIDE 9]
Illustrative scenarios
Not market forecasts
Conservative: 30% occupancy / ₦35k ADR
Base: 45% occupancy / ₦50k ADR
Upside: 60% occupancy / ₦70k ADR
See workbook for formulas, sensitivity and five-year model
9

[SLIDE 10]
Governance & control
Public-asset accountability
Executive sponsor + cross-functional steering committee
Finance + Procurement + Legal + Property/RPMCL + ICT + Audit
Daily revenue reconciliation
Asset inventory and room readiness certification
10

[SLIDE 11]
Digital platform
Booking, payment, operations and audit
Booking and availability
Payment reference and invoicing
Housekeeping / maintenance status
Guest record and feedback
Revenue dashboard and audit trail
MFA / RBAC / DPIA / cybersecurity
11

[SLIDE 12]
Implementation roadmap
Stage-gated delivery
Stage 0: mandate
Stage 1: legal + asset discovery
Stage 2: market study
Stage 3: business case
Stage 4: design/procurement
Stage 5: refurbishment
Stage 6: technology
Stage 7: commissioning
Stage 8: pilot
Stage 9: scale
12

[SLIDE 13]
Decision requested
Immediate management authorisations
Approve formal feasibility/discovery
Nominate sponsor and project team
Authorise site/technical survey
Require Legal/Property/Procurement route assessment
Return with pilot investment paper before major capital commitment
13

[SLIDE 14]
Close
North-star proposition
The proposition is not “rent the chalets.”
The proposition is “commercialise an NRC accommodation asset through a controlled, auditable hospitality model.”
Success = net revenue + asset preservation + service quality + governance
14

MEMORANDUM
1. Purpose
This memorandum requests the Managing Director's in-principle approval to develop a pilot commercialisation programme for the 12 chalet units located at Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos, currently under-utilised and requiring renovation.
2. Background
The chalet facility represents an NRC asset that is presently generating no revenue and continuing to depreciate. The Nigerian Railway Corporation Act gives NRC express power to provide hotels, hostels, living accommodation and places of refreshment, and Railway Property Management Company Limited (RPMCL) already carries a mandate to commercialise NRC land and buildings for optimum revenue generation. This proposal fits directly within that existing statutory and institutional framework.
3. Proposal
It is proposed that NRC undertake a professionally structured pilot commercialisation programme for the chalets — refurbishing an initial 5 of the 12 units to a serviced-accommodation standard and testing occupancy, achievable tariff and net operating margin over a defined period — before deciding whether to commit capital to the remaining 7 units.
A full Master Blueprint accompanies this memorandum, together with a Financial & Asset Model workbook, an Operating SOPs & Governance Charter, and an Executive Presentation. All financial figures in these materials are clearly marked as indicative and pending verification through the physical inspection and market study described below.
4. Specific Approval Requested
Approval, in principle, of the chalet commercialisation concept as an NRC revenue-generating asset initiative.
A mandate to conduct a physical inspection, legal/title review and market benchmarking exercise for the 12 units (Phase 1 of the attached roadmap).
Constitution of a Project Steering Committee, with representation from Finance, Legal, Procurement, Internal Audit, ICT and Estate/Property, and appointment of an Executive Sponsor.
In-principle support for a 5-unit pilot programme, subject to the findings of Phase 1–3 and a finalised business case being brought back for approval.
No lease, concession, management contract or other binding commercial instrument is being sought at this stage. This memorandum requests only the mandate to investigate, cost and structure the opportunity properly.
5. Why This Structure
NRC retains ownership of the asset throughout.
NRC approves the business model before any capital is committed.
NRC controls governance and revenue, with Internal Audit visibility built in from the outset.
Any operating arrangement (direct operation, management contract, revenue-share or concession) is selected only through the applicable procurement process, on Legal's advice as to the correct instrument.
6. Indicative Financial Case (Subject to Verification)
The attached Financial & Asset Model estimates a total refurbishment CAPEX of approximately ₦111.5 million for all 12 units (of which approximately ₦46.5 million relates to the 5-unit pilot), against an indicative Base Scenario Net Operating Income rising from approximately ₦46.1 million in Year 1 to approximately ₦114.5 million by Year 3. These figures are built on placeholder tariff and cost assumptions and must not be relied upon for a funding decision until confirmed by the Phase 1 physical inspection, a market tariff benchmarking study, and actual utility/staffing cost data from NRC Estate and Finance.
7. Recommendation
It is recommended that the Managing Director approve the four items requested in Section 4 above, enabling the project to proceed to Phase 1 (Asset & Legal Discovery) without committing any refurbishment capital at this stage.
Respectfully submitted,
_________________________________

### DOCUMENT: `05_NRC_CHALET/NRC_Chalet_Evidence_Validation_Pack_2026__EXTRACTED/NRC_Chalet_Evidence_Market_Validation_Addendum.docx`

**Size:** 41,366 bytes

NIGERIAN RAILWAY CORPORATION
CHALET COMMERCIALISATION - EVIDENCE & MARKET VALIDATION ADDENDUM
Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos | 12 Units | Evidence Update | 4 September 2026
Internal / Restricted - Commercial-in-Confidence
1. Executive finding
The previous draft had the right business shape but several statements were too easy to challenge because they were based on placeholders or broad market claims. Current research supports a stronger, more defensible pitch: NRC has a documented commercial hospitality precedent at the same Ebute-Metta compound; current local competitors visibly price hotel rooms around N27,500-N55,000/night; current Yaba one-bedroom short-let listings show a much wider serviced-apartment band, including N65,000-N130,000/day examples and a portal-reported average of N120,000/day. The correct conclusion is not that NRC can charge N55,000 or N120,000. The correct conclusion is that a N55,000 working Base ADR is plausible enough to test, while the final tariff must be established through a controlled local benchmark and pilot.
2. What is now corroborated
Same-compound NRC precedent
In September 2021, NRC opened a 40-bed commercial Railway Guest House at its Ebute-Metta station. NAN reporting put the project cost at about N320 million and stated that Ojez Group was selected from more than 30 bidders to manage the facility. This is the strongest narrative anchor for the proposal because it demonstrates that NRC has already used the basic model of commercialising hospitality assets at this location. It does not prove that the 12 chalets will perform similarly.
Current Ojez price ladder
Hotels.ng currently lists Ojez Hotel & Suites in Ebute Metta from N27,500 to N55,000 per night across several room categories. The Ojez company website still identifies O’JEZ Hotels & Suites as part of its hospitality business and places an operating contact at the Railway Recreation Center, Ebute-Metta.
Current Yaba serviced-apartment market
Nigeria Property Centre currently shows 110 one-bedroom short-let listings in Yaba as of 4 September 2026, with a portal-reported average of N120,000/day. Individual observed furnished/serviced examples include N65,000/day in Alagomeji and N130,000/day on Muritala Muhammed Way. These are asking/listing prices, not audited achieved revenue.
Lagos market scale
Edala Development research, as reported by Nairametrics, estimated Lagos short-let market revenue at N281.03bn in 2025 from 6,398 tracked units. The report describes a maturing market with continuing demand but increasing competition and supply.
Occupancy evidence
A September 2026 Nairametrics report quoted Edala Development’s COO as saying occupancy across Edala properties ranges from about 59% to 80%, with stronger demand in December-February. The same report states that industry-wide data are limited. Therefore the prior statement that Lagos shortlets “average 51% occupancy” should be removed unless a primary source is obtained.
3. What should be removed or softened from the earlier draft
“Lagos shortlet occupancy citywide averages around 51%.” - REMOVE. Current evidence found does not substantiate this as an industry-wide Lagos average.
“The ₦55,000 Base ADR is verified.” - DO NOT SAY THIS. Say it is a working hypothesis supported by the local price ladder and to be validated by a formal benchmark and pilot.
“Renovation costs are ₦150,000-₦250,000 per sqm.” - DO NOT use as the project’s cost basis. Online construction/renovation guides are too generic; the business case should use a measured QS BOQ. Current new-build cost commentary shows wide variation by specification, which reinforces the need for a project-specific BOQ.
“40%-60% occupancy is conservative against the Lagos average.” - REFRAME. It is a planning scenario that should be tested against the pilot; it is not directly benchmarked to a verified citywide statistic.
4. Recommended evidence-backed planning assumptions
5. Plain-English meaning of the financial terms
ADR: Average Daily Rate: the average price charged for one occupied unit for one night.
Occupancy: The percentage of available nights actually sold.
CAPEX: One-time investment to renovate, equip and prepare the units.
OPEX: Recurring running costs: staff, power, water, housekeeping, security, internet, maintenance, etc.
NOI: Net Operating Income: operating revenue less operating costs, before financing and other corporate-level items defined in the model.
Break-even occupancy: The occupancy level at which operating revenue covers the modelled operating cost base.
Payback: How long the incremental cash generation would take to recover the renovation investment under the specified assumptions.
NPV: Net Present Value: today’s value of future cash flows after applying a discount rate for time and risk.
IRR: Internal Rate of Return: the discount rate that makes the project’s NPV equal to zero; it is a return metric, not a guaranteed interest rate.
Management contract: NRC retains ownership and hires a professional operator to run the facility for a defined contractual fee / arrangement.
Concession: A longer-term commercial arrangement that can transfer more operating rights/control to a private party and therefore requires more careful legal/procurement structuring.
6. What the MD should hear - not a technical lecture
“NRC already has a precedent at this exact compound: the Railway Guest House was commercialised and professionally managed. I am proposing that we investigate whether the 12 existing chalets can be converted into a smaller serviced-accommodation product. I am not asking Management to approve a lease or hand over the asset. I am asking for permission to inspect the property, establish the legal route, benchmark the market, cost the renovation properly and test five units. If the numbers work, Management decides whether to scale.”
7. Evidence discipline for the next revision
Use “listed/asking price” whenever referring to portal rates. Do not call listing prices “market achieved rates.”
Use the same-compound NRC/Ojez precedent as evidence of organisational feasibility, not evidence of financial performance for the chalets.
Use the current Yaba listing data to support a price-range discussion, not a promise of tariff.
Use actual pilot bookings, occupancy, costs and guest feedback to replace scenario assumptions after launch.
Replace all renovation placeholders with a measured Quantity Surveyor BOQ and contractor market testing before capital approval.
8. Sources
S1 - Pulse Nigeria / NAN - NRC builds 40-bed hotel worth N320m at Ebute-Metta station (2021-09-02)
https://www.pulse.ng/story/nrc-builds-40-bed-hotel-worth-n320m-at-ebute-metta-station-2024081821120168126
S2 - OJEZ Entertainment Limited - Corporate / Hospitality profile (2026)
https://ojezgroup.com.ng/
S3 - Hotels.ng - Ojez Hotel & Suites - current room rates (2026-09-04)
https://hotels.ng/hotel/1441395-ojez-hotel-suites
S4 - Nigeria Property Centre - 1 Bedroom Short Let Flats in Yaba, Lagos (2026-09-04)
https://nigeriapropertycentre.com/for-rent/short-let/flats-apartments/lagos/yaba/showtype?bedrooms=1
S5 - Nigeria Property Centre - 1 Bedroom Short Let Flats in Yaba, Lagos - observed comps (2026-08-27)
https://nigeriapropertycentre.com/for-rent/short-let/flats-apartments/lagos/yaba/3643531-1-bedroom-loft-apartment

[WORKSHEET: Risk Register]
RISK REGISTER |  |  |  |  | 
Chalet Asset Commercialisation Programme — Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos |  |  |  |  | 
# | Risk | Category | Impact | Mitigation / Response | Owner
1 | Legal restriction on dealing with NRC immovable property (Ministerial approval requirement) | Legal | Critical | Obtain Legal Department opinion on the applicable statutory authority and required approvals before any commercial arrangement is finalised. | Legal Lead
2 | Wrong operating model selected (Direct / Management Contract / Revenue-Share / Concession) | Commercial | High | Complete the weighted comparative feasibility study (Blueprint §65–66) before recommending a model to the MD. | Commercial Lead
3 | Refurbishment cost underestimated at Ebute Metta due to lack of physical inspection | Financial | High | Commission a Quantity Surveyor condition survey (Grade A–E per §14) for all 12 units before finalising CAPEX. | Estate/Property Lead
4 | Low occupancy — market does not respond as modelled | Commercial | High | Validate demand via the 5-unit pilot programme before committing full-portfolio CAPEX; use conservative scenario for approval purposes. | Project Manager
5 | Power cost (grid/generator) erodes margin at Ebute Metta | Operational | High | Complete an energy strategy assessment (grid / generator / solar / hybrid) and track cost-per-occupied-night from Month 1 of the pilot. | Facilities Lead
6 | Theft or loss of NRC assets (furniture, appliances, fittings) | Asset Protection | Medium/High | Implement per-unit asset inventory with Asset IDs, checked at every check-in/check-out (Blueprint §44). | Operations Manager
7 | Revenue leakage — cash collected but not banked, or bookings without payment | Governance | Critical | Digital payment and reconciliation architecture with no cash-leakage design (Blueprint §41–43); Internal Audit dashboard access. | Finance Lead / Internal Audit
8 | Poor guest service damaging the NRC brand | Reputational | High | Adopt the NRC Housekeeping SOP and Guest Journey standards; track Guest Satisfaction Index monthly. | Hospitality Lead
9 | Procurement process delays or challenge | Procurement | Critical | Engage Procurement early to confirm the applicable route under the Public Procurement Act before appointing any operator. | Procurement Lead
10 | Property title / land-use dispute at the Ebute Metta compound | Legal / Property | Critical | Confirm title and land-use status with NRC Estate/RPMCL before public marketing of the accommodation product. | Estate/Property Lead
11 | Cybersecurity — booking, payment and guest-data systems compromised | Technology | High | MFA, role-based access control, encryption, audit logs and regular vulnerability testing on the booking/PMS platform. | ICT Lead
12 | Guest data-protection breach (Nigeria Data Protection Act) | Compliance | High | Adopt a guest-data privacy notice, retention schedule, access controls and breach procedure before go-live. | Legal / ICT Lead
13 | Vendor/operator dependency under a management contract or concession | Commercial | High | Build clear contract and exit/termination controls into any third-party operating agreement. | Legal / Commercial Lead
14 | Deferred maintenance neglect after initial refurbishment | Asset | High | Adopt a preventive maintenance schedule and fund the maintenance reserve (5% of gross revenue) from Month 1. | Facilities Lead
15 | Flood / environmental exposure typical of low-lying Lagos railway-corridor sites | Environmental | Medium | Include a site drainage and flood-risk assessment in the Phase 1 physical inspection at Ebute Metta. | Estate/Property Lead
16 | Perception risk — proposal seen as a personal commercial request rather than an NRC initiative | Governance | Medium | Frame and route the proposal as an NRC-owned pilot commercialisation programme with governance-first positioning (Blueprint §82–84). | Executive Sponsor

IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP — PHASE 0 TO PHASE 9 |  |  |  |  | 
Indicative timeline; to be finalised with the Project Steering Committee. |  |  |  |  | 
Phase | Name | Key Deliverables | Indicative Timing | Owner | Gate / Approval
0 | Mandate | Formal project establishment; Executive Sponsor and Steering Committee constituted | Month 1 | Executive Sponsor | MD approval to proceed

2 | Market Feasibility | Target customer segmentation; competitor/comparable tariff benchmarking; demand and seasonality assessment | Months 2–3 | Commercial Lead | Market study signed off
3 | Business & Financial Case | CAPEX/OPEX, revenue, occupancy, pricing, break-even, ROI/NPV/IRR and sensitivity analysis finalised | Month 3 | Finance Lead | Business case approved by Steering Committee
4 | Operating Model | Staffing, housekeeping, security, maintenance, procurement and reservations model defined | Month 3 | Hospitality Lead | Operating model approved
5 | Refurbishment Design | Architectural, engineering and Quantity Surveyor package for pilot units | Months 3–4 | Estate/Property Lead | Design sign-off

8 | Pilot (3–5 units) | Pilot units refurbished and launched; 10 pilot questions (§78) tracked monthly | Months 4–7 | Project Manager | MD/Steering Committee review of pilot results

### DOCUMENT: `05_NRC_CHALET/NRC_Chalet_Evidence_Validation_Pack_2026__EXTRACTED/NRC_Chalet_Plain_English_MD_Pitch_Guide.docx`

NIGERIAN RAILWAY CORPORATION
NRC CHALET - PLAIN-ENGLISH MD PITCH & QUESTION PREPARATION GUIDE
Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos | 12 Units | Evidence Update | 4 September 2026
Internal / Restricted - Commercial-in-Confidence
1. The idea in one sentence
“Take 12 NRC chalet units in Ebute Metta that currently need renovation, test whether five can be converted into professionally managed one-bedroom serviced suites, and only scale if the pilot proves demand, service quality, governance and net revenue.”
2. Why this is not just an idea
NRC has a documented precedent at the same compound. In September 2021, the Corporation opened a 40-bed commercial Railway Guest House at Ebute-Metta and selected Ojez Group from more than 30 bidders to manage it. That is evidence of organisational precedent. It is not proof that the chalets will make money; the pilot must prove that.
3. The three numbers you should be ready to explain
Why ₦55,000 per night? Because current Ojez hotel listings in Ebute Metta extend up to ₦55,000/night, while current furnished/serviced one-bedroom Yaba listings include ₦65,000 and ₦130,000/day examples. ₦55,000 is therefore a testable working hypothesis for a fully equipped one-bedroom suite, not a final tariff.
Why 40% occupancy in Year 1? It is a deliberately moderate planning scenario, not a claim about Lagos. Current industry-wide occupancy data are weak. We will test actual occupancy with five pilot units.
Why ₦111.5m CAPEX? It is a placeholder model output based on an assumed per-unit renovation amount. It is not a QS estimate. No capital decision should rely on it until the 12 units are surveyed and a BOQ is produced.
4. Questions the MD may ask - and how to answer
What evidence says people will pay? Current comparable listings show an observable local price ladder from approximately ₦27,500 hotel rooms in the same area to ₦65,000-₦130,000 examples for furnished/serviced one-bedroom units in Yaba. The pilot converts this into actual demand evidence.
Why should NRC do this instead of leasing the property? The first question is not lease versus operate. The first question is which legally permissible model gives NRC the best combination of control, risk and net revenue. Four models should be compared before selection.
What stops revenue leakage? A digital booking-to-bank chain: booking, approved tariff, invoice, payment, bank, accounting, revenue report and audit. No informal staff discounts and no personal accounts.
What if the market does not respond? The five-unit pilot is the protection. NRC commits to testing first and scaling only after a formal gate.
What about legal/procurement issues? No lease, concession or management contract is being requested at this stage. Legal, Estate/RPMCL, Procurement and Finance first determine the permissible commercial route.
Why not renovate all 12 now? Because the business case is still uncertain. A pilot preserves capital discipline and produces real operating data before full rollout.
5. The jargon translated
ADR: Average Daily Rate: the average price charged for one occupied unit for one night.
Occupancy: The percentage of available nights actually sold.
CAPEX: One-time investment to renovate, equip and prepare the units.
OPEX: Recurring running costs: staff, power, water, housekeeping, security, internet, maintenance, etc.
NOI: Net Operating Income: operating revenue less operating costs, before financing and other corporate-level items defined in the model.
Break-even occupancy: The occupancy level at which operating revenue covers the modelled operating cost base.
Payback: How long the incremental cash generation would take to recover the renovation investment under the specified assumptions.
NPV: Net Present Value: today’s value of future cash flows after applying a discount rate for time and risk.
IRR: Internal Rate of Return: the discount rate that makes the project’s NPV equal to zero; it is a return metric, not a guaranteed interest rate.
Management contract: NRC retains ownership and hires a professional operator to run the facility for a defined contractual fee / arrangement.
Concession: A longer-term commercial arrangement that can transfer more operating rights/control to a private party and therefore requires more careful legal/procurement structuring.
6. What not to say
“The project will make ₦114m NOI by Year 3.” Say instead: “The current model indicates that outcome under the placeholder Base Scenario; we need to validate the tariff, costs and occupancy.”
“Lagos occupancy is 51%.” Do not use unless a primary source is obtained.
“Renovation will cost ₦9.3m per unit.” Say: “The current model carries ₦9.295m per unit as a placeholder; the QS BOQ will replace it.”
“Ojez proves we will succeed.” Say: “Ojez proves NRC has already used a commercial hospitality model at the same compound.”
7. Your 30-second close
“I am not asking you to commit NRC to a hotel business today. I am asking for permission to properly investigate an existing asset that is currently under-used. We already have a precedent for commercial hospitality at Ebute-Metta. Let us inspect the 12 units, establish the legal and procurement route, benchmark the market, cost five units properly and run a controlled pilot. If the evidence says it works, Management can then decide whether to scale.”
8. Sources used in this guide
S1 - Pulse Nigeria / NAN - NRC builds 40-bed hotel worth N320m at Ebute-Metta station (2021-09-02)
https://www.pulse.ng/story/nrc-builds-40-bed-hotel-worth-n320m-at-ebute-metta-station-2024081821120168126
S2 - OJEZ Entertainment Limited - Corporate / Hospitality profile (2026)
https://ojezgroup.com.ng/
S3 - Hotels.ng - Ojez Hotel & Suites - current room rates (2026-09-04)
https://hotels.ng/hotel/1441395-ojez-hotel-suites
S4 - Nigeria Property Centre - 1 Bedroom Short Let Flats in Yaba, Lagos (2026-09-04)
https://nigeriapropertycentre.com/for-rent/short-let/flats-apartments/lagos/yaba/showtype?bedrooms=1
S5 - Nigeria Property Centre - 1 Bedroom Short Let Flats in Yaba, Lagos - observed comps (2026-08-27)
https://nigeriapropertycentre.com/for-rent/short-let/flats-apartments/lagos/yaba/3643531-1-bedroom-loft-apartment

THE OPPORTUNITY
From an under-utilised asset to recurring NRC revenue
THE PROBLEM
12 chalet units at Railway Compound, Ebute Metta sit vacant and generate no revenue.
The facility requires renovation — every month of delay adds to the eventual cost.
Left as-is, it is a depreciating public asset, not a source of internally generated revenue (IGR).
THE OPPORTUNITY
Same 12 units, professionally refurbished, become NRC Executive Serviced Suites.
The unit layout (entrance → lobby → bedroom/ensuite → living-dining → kitchen) suits a one-bedroom serviced product with no structural rework.
Fits directly within RPMCL's existing mandate to commercialise NRC land and buildings for optimum revenue.
Lagos mainland corporate, transit and NRC-ecosystem demand is well matched to Ebute Metta's location.
“Convert an under-utilised public asset into a professionally managed revenue-producing asset — without compromising NRC's statutory, fiduciary or governance obligations.”

The Nigerian Railway Corporation Act expressly empowers NRC to provide hotels, hostels, living accommodation and places of refreshment for passengers and other persons — this is not a new philosophy, but a direct statutory anchor for the chalet concept.
RPMCL already carries a mandate to manage and commercialise NRC land and buildings for optimum revenue generation — this project sits inside that existing strategy.

Chalet Asset Commercialisation Programme — Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos |  |  |  |  | 
# | Risk | Category | Impact | Mitigation / Response | Owner
1 | Legal restriction on dealing with NRC immovable property (Ministerial approval requirement) | Legal | Critical | Obtain Legal Department opinion on the applicable statutory authority and required approvals before any commercial arrangement is finalised. | Legal Lead
2 | Wrong operating model selected (Direct / Management Contract / Revenue-Share / Concession) | Commercial | High | Complete the weighted comparative feasibility study (Blueprint §65–66) before recommending a model to the MD. | Commercial Lead
3 | Refurbishment cost underestimated at Ebute Metta due to lack of physical inspection | Financial | High | Commission a Quantity Surveyor condition survey (Grade A–E per §14) for all 12 units before finalising CAPEX. | Estate/Property Lead
4 | Low occupancy — market does not respond as modelled | Commercial | High | Validate demand via the 5-unit pilot programme before committing full-portfolio CAPEX; use conservative scenario for approval purposes. | Project Manager
5 | Power cost (grid/generator) erodes margin at Ebute Metta | Operational | High | Complete an energy strategy assessment (grid / generator / solar / hybrid) and track cost-per-occupied-night from Month 1 of the pilot. | Facilities Lead
6 | Theft or loss of NRC assets (furniture, appliances, fittings) | Asset Protection | Medium/High | Implement per-unit asset inventory with Asset IDs, checked at every check-in/check-out (Blueprint §44). | Operations Manager
7 | Revenue leakage — cash collected but not banked, or bookings without payment | Governance | Critical | Digital payment and reconciliation architecture with no cash-leakage design (Blueprint §41–43); Internal Audit dashboard access. | Finance Lead / Internal Audit
8 | Poor guest service damaging the NRC brand | Reputational | High | Adopt the NRC Housekeeping SOP and Guest Journey standards; track Guest Satisfaction Index monthly. | Hospitality Lead
9 | Procurement process delays or challenge | Procurement | Critical | Engage Procurement early to confirm the applicable route under the Public Procurement Act before appointing any operator. | Procurement Lead
10 | Property title / land-use dispute at the Ebute Metta compound | Legal / Property | Critical | Confirm title and land-use status with NRC Estate/RPMCL before public marketing of the accommodation product. | Estate/Property Lead
11 | Cybersecurity — booking, payment and guest-data systems compromised | Technology | High | MFA, role-based access control, encryption, audit logs and regular vulnerability testing on the booking/PMS platform. | ICT Lead
12 | Guest data-protection breach (Nigeria Data Protection Act) | Compliance | High | Adopt a guest-data privacy notice, retention schedule, access controls and breach procedure before go-live. | Legal / ICT Lead
13 | Vendor/operator dependency under a management contract or concession | Commercial | High | Build clear contract and exit/termination controls into any third-party operating agreement. | Legal / Commercial Lead
14 | Deferred maintenance neglect after initial refurbishment | Asset | High | Adopt a preventive maintenance schedule and fund the maintenance reserve (5% of gross revenue) from Month 1. | Facilities Lead
15 | Flood / environmental exposure typical of low-lying Lagos railway-corridor sites | Environmental | Medium | Include a site drainage and flood-risk assessment in the Phase 1 physical inspection at Ebute Metta. | Estate/Property Lead
16 | Perception risk — proposal seen as a personal commercial request rather than an NRC initiative | Governance | Medium | Frame and route the proposal as an NRC-owned pilot commercialisation programme with governance-first positioning (Blueprint §82–84). | Executive Sponsor

NIGERIAN RAILWAY CORPORATION
NRC CHALET ASSET COMMERCIALISATION,
HOSPITALITY DEVELOPMENT & REVENUE
OPTIMISATION MASTER BLUEPRINT
