Refurbishment Strategy, Technology Architecture, Governance & Implementation Roadmap
Chalet Facility — Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos
12 Units  |  Condition: Requires Renovation  |  Pilot-First Implementation Strategy
Contents
(If this table does not display page numbers, right-click it and choose "Update Field" — or press F9 with the cursor inside it.)
1.  Executive Summary
There is an opportunity to undertake a professionally structured pilot for the commercial utilisation of NRC's accommodation assets at Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos, with the objective of generating additional revenue for the Corporation, preserving the underlying assets, and establishing a transparent operating model that can be scaled if the pilot proves financially and operationally viable.
The facility comprises 12 chalet units currently under-utilised and requiring renovation. This document proposes their transformation into a professionally managed NRC Executive Serviced Accommodation product — branded NRC Executive Serviced Suites — generating nightly, weekly, monthly and corporate accommodation revenue, supported by ancillary services (meetings, laundry, food & beverage, transfers).
This is deliberately framed as a public-asset commercialisation and revenue-optimisation initiative, not as a private rental arrangement. It rests on NRC's own statutory authority to provide hotels, hostels, living accommodation and places of refreshment, and aligns with the mandate already held by Railway Property Management Company Limited (RPMCL) to commercialise NRC land and buildings for optimum revenue generation.
Key Recommendation
Adopt a hybrid NRC Direct Operation / Management Contract model, retaining NRC ownership and commercial control while engaging professional hospitality management capability — beginning with a 5-unit pilot before committing capital to the remaining 7 units.
Headline Figures (Indicative — Pending Verification)
The accompanying Financial & Asset Model produces the following indicative Base Scenario figures for the full 12-unit portfolio. These are planning-stage estimates built on placeholder tariff and cost assumptions — see Section 15 and the workbook's Assumptions tab for the caveats that apply before any of these numbers are relied upon for a funding decision.
Total indicative CAPEX for the full 12-unit refurbishment is ₦111,540,000 (approximately ₦9,295,000 per unit), of which the 5-unit pilot requires approximately ₦46,475,000. Because the return profile the model produces is unusually strong, it should be treated as a hypothesis for the pilot to test — not a figure to present to the MD as verified. Section 15 sets out exactly what must be confirmed (market tariffs, condition-survey costs, actual utility and staffing costs) before this model can support a capital-commitment decision.
What This Document Asks the MD to Approve
Approval, in principle, of the chalet commercialisation concept as an NRC revenue-generating asset initiative.
A mandate to conduct Phase 1 (Asset & Legal Discovery) — physical inspection of the 12 Ebute Metta units, legal/title confirmation, and a market benchmarking exercise.
Constitution of a Project Steering Committee and appointment of an Executive Sponsor.
In-principle support for a 5-unit pilot programme, subject to the Phase 1–3 findings and a final business case.
This is not a request to hand the chalets to any individual to operate. It is a proposal that NRC own the asset, approve the business model, control governance and revenue, and select an appropriate operating arrangement through the applicable procurement process.
2.  Problem / Opportunity
The Problem
The 12 chalet units at Railway Compound, Ebute Metta are currently under-utilised, generating no material revenue, and require renovation. Left as they are, they represent a depreciating public asset — a cost centre rather than a source of internally generated revenue (IGR) for the Corporation.
The Opportunity
Converted and professionally managed, the same 12 units can become a source of recurring revenue for NRC, in a market segment — short-stay and corporate serviced accommodation — with established demand in Lagos. The physical configuration described for the units (detached unit → bedroom/ensuite → transition lobby → visitor WC → living/dining → service lobby → kitchen) is well suited to a one-bedroom serviced-suite product without structural reconfiguration.
Why Now
The units are deteriorating further the longer they remain unused, increasing the eventual cost of rehabilitation.
NRC's own property ecosystem (RPMCL) already carries a mandate to commercialise land and buildings for optimum revenue generation — this proposal fits directly within that existing strategy rather than requiring a new philosophy.
Lagos's serviced-accommodation and short-let market has continued to grow, driven by corporate travel, transit demand and a shortage of quality mid-market stock outside the traditional hotel districts.
The central thesis: convert an under-utilised public asset from a cost centre into a professionally managed revenue-producing asset — without compromising NRC's statutory, fiduciary, procurement, property, safety, financial or governance obligations.
3.  Strategic Alignment
This proposal is explicitly positioned within four simultaneous objectives, so that it reads as an organisational initiative rather than a personal request:
NRC's Finance & Accounts Department is responsible for revenue accounting, revenue reporting, financial controls and IGR monitoring, while Internal Audit monitors revenues, ensures earnings are banked, and conducts post-audit / value-for-money reviews of NRC facilities and assets. This proposal is deliberately designed around those existing governance functions rather than as an informal private-business arrangement sitting outside them.
4.  Legal & Institutional Framework
Statutory Basis
The Nigerian Railway Corporation Act expressly gives NRC power to provide hotels, hostels, other living accommodation and places of refreshment for passengers and other persons. This gives the chalet concept a direct statutory anchor rather than treating it as an unrelated side business.
A Necessary Caution
The same Act contains restrictions on dealing with NRC immovable property: in particular, the Corporation cannot alienate, mortgage, charge or demise certain immovable property without the written approval of the Minister. This proposal therefore does not describe the intended arrangement as a 'lease' or 'concession' until Legal, Property and Procurement authorities have determined precisely what legal instrument is appropriate for the Ebute Metta chalets.
There is a material difference between NRC itself operating the accommodation, NRC engaging a private hotel operator under a management contract, NRC granting a lease, NRC entering a revenue-sharing arrangement, NRC creating a joint venture / SPV, and NRC granting a concession. These are not interchangeable, and the correct route must be confirmed by Legal and Procurement before any operator is engaged (see Section 9 and Section 16).
Who Owns / Controls the Asset
The asset sits within a clear institutional chain: Federal Government → NRC → NRC Asset/Property → the Ebute Metta Chalet Facility. The question of who is legally authorised to commercialise it — NRC directly, an authorised NRC subsidiary, RPMCL, an approved external operator, or a public-private structure — must be confirmed in Phase 1, not assumed.
RPMCL's own published mandate is to manage presently commercialised and potentially commercialisable NRC lands, buildings and quarries nationwide. That establishes that the organisational relationship between this project and RPMCL must be investigated, not that RPMCL should automatically operate these particular chalets.
Procurement Framework
The commercial structure ultimately selected must be consistent with the Public Procurement Act, which recognises rental, lease, licences and tenancies among the modes of dealing with public property, and imposes formal valuation and process requirements on such arrangements. The Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) publishes the standard bidding documents and procurement manuals that will govern whichever route is chosen (see Section 16).
Data Protection
Guest information collected through the booking and stay process is personal data. The Nigeria Data Protection Act imposes duties on organisations regarding the data of customers, employees, guests and visitors in their custody — this has direct implications for the design of the booking platform (Section 13) and requires a guest-data privacy notice, retention schedule and access-control policy before go-live.
5.  Current Asset Assessment
This section summarises the physical asset as currently known. Full detail — GPS coordinates, floor areas, utilities and a unit-by-unit condition grade — is captured in the Asset Register tab of the accompanying Financial & Asset Model workbook, and must be completed through a physical site inspection before the business case is finalised.
Indicative Unit Layout
The description supplied for the units — a detached one-bedroom structure moving from entrance through a transition lobby into the bedroom/ensuite and living/dining space, with a service lobby leading to the kitchen — creates a natural hospitality flow without requiring structural reconfiguration. The schematic below represents that flow; it is not a measured drawing and must be replaced with an architectural survey during Phase 1.
Figure 1 — Indicative unit layout (schematic, not to scale). Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos.
Condition Grading Methodology
Each unit should be graded A through E once inspected, so that capital is not spent equally across units that need very different levels of work:
Grade A — Ready: minimal work required.
Grade B — Light refurbishment: painting, furnishings, minor repairs.
Grade C — Major refurbishment: plumbing / electrical / roofing (provisional grade applied to all 12 units pending inspection, consistent with the brief that the facility 'needs renovation').
Grade D — Structural rehabilitation: significant capital expenditure.
Grade E — Economically obsolete: rebuild / repurpose decision required.
Photographic Record
Placeholder images accompany this toolkit and should be replaced with actual site photography (exterior, interior, kitchen, bathroom) for each of the 12 units before the proposal is presented to the MD.
Placeholder — exterior photograph (to be replaced).
6.  Market Analysis
A dedicated market benchmarking study is required before tariffs are finalised (see Section 15's caution against setting price by guessing). This section sets out the scope of that study.
Benchmarking Scope
Comparable serviced apartments and guest houses on the Lagos mainland, particularly within reach of Ebute Metta, Yaba, Ikeja and the Apapa–Ebute Metta commercial corridor.
Budget and mid-market hotels serving corporate and transit travellers in the same catchment.
Weekday vs weekend pricing patterns, and seasonal demand variation.
Occupancy benchmarks for comparable short-stay stock.
The amenity, security and transport-proximity factors that justify a premium or require a discount relative to comparable stock.
Location Considerations Specific to Ebute Metta
Ebute Metta is a historic railway and commercial hub on the Lagos mainland with strong transport connectivity (rail, road and proximity to the Mainland–Island corridor). This favours corporate, transit and NRC-ecosystem demand over a leisure/tourism positioning. The market study should test this assumption directly rather than assume it.
The location's characteristics — including its lower-lying, railway-corridor terrain — should also inform the Phase 1 physical inspection, including a basic drainage and flood-risk review (see the Risk Register).
7.  Proposed Product
The physical description supplied for the units is more commercially identifiable as luxury one-bedroom serviced bungalows than as traditional chalets. 'NRC Chalets' is retained as the internal/public asset name, while the accommodation is commercially branded NRC Executive Serviced Suites — avoiding a misleading 'chalet' category for customers while preserving the familiar internal terminology.
The 'Walk-In' Standard
The guiding design principle: a guest should be able to arrive carrying only clothes and personal belongings — not furniture, kitchen equipment, bedding or household necessities.
Unit Standard
Product Tiers
Not every unit need be identical. The indicative product mix modelled in the Financial & Asset Model is:
Standard Executive Suite — 8 units — one-bedroom furnished unit.
Premium Executive Suite — 3 units — upgraded furniture, appliances and bedding, priced at a premium to Standard.
Corporate Long-Stay Suite — 1 unit — additional workspace and laundry/kitchen provisioning, priced at a discount to the nightly-equivalent Standard rate to reward longer stays.
This tiering allows price discrimination and demand segmentation without constructing additional units, and should be revisited once the market study and physical condition survey are complete.
8.  Customer Segmentation
NRC ecosystem — staff, retired officers (where policy permits), official visitors, contractors, consultants, railway partners, visiting government officials.
Corporate — business travellers, project teams, consultants, corporate visitors to the Lagos mainland and Apapa port corridor.
Transit — rail and other travellers and railway-related visitors, given the Ebute Metta location's rail connectivity.
General market — families, short-stay guests, event visitors.
Institutional — government agencies, NGOs, development organisations and companies requiring accommodation blocks.
The product should be positioned as Professionally Managed Serviced Accommodation — deliberately avoiding an 'Airbnb for NRC' description, which would understate the intended institutional and corporate positioning.
9.  Operating Models
Before selecting a route, four operating models should be tested against the legal, financial and governance criteria set out in this document. None should be assumed at the outset — least of all a private-operator arrangement.
Model A — NRC Direct Operation
NRC owns and directly manages the accommodation. 100% of approved gross accommodation revenue belongs to NRC, subject to operating expenses. Maximum control and visibility, but NRC bears full operating risk and requires in-house hospitality expertise and staffing.
Model B — Management Contract
NRC retains the asset; an approved hospitality operator provides operational management (bookings, housekeeping, reception, guest services, maintenance) for a fee. NRC retains ownership and economic interest while leveraging professional hospitality capability.
Model C — Revenue-Sharing Arrangement
An operator manages the facility and NRC receives an agreed share of revenue or operating profit under a properly procured and legally approved formula (gross revenue → approved operating costs → net operating revenue → split between NRC share, operator share and a maintenance reserve). Attractive but requires sophisticated contract controls.
Model D — Concession / Other Commercial Structure
A private party operates and invests under a longer-term arrangement, bringing private capital and professional operations at the cost of far greater property, procurement, contractual, approval, valuation and termination complexity.
10.  Recommended Commercial Model
Without the benefit of the completed physical inspection, legal opinion and market study, this document sets out a preliminary architectural preference only — not a final recommendation.
Preliminary preference: a Model A + Model B hybrid — NRC retains asset ownership, commercial oversight and control, while engaging professional hospitality management capability to operate the facility.
The rationale: the principal objective is not to hand the chalets to someone to run, but to make them commercially productive while retaining NRC's control over an important public asset. This framing makes it easier to demonstrate that the project is about asset optimisation, not asset disposal.
Weighted Scoring Framework
The final business case should score each of the four models against weighted criteria, for example:
Legal viability — 20%
Financial return — 25%
NRC control — 15%
Implementation risk — 10%
Operational capability — 10%
Capital requirement — 10%
Scalability — 5%
Strategic fit — 5%
These weights are illustrative and should be reviewed and approved by the Steering Committee before being applied.
11.  Refurbishment Plan
The CAPEX Plan tab of the Financial & Asset Model workbook sets out an indicative per-unit refurbishment cost build-up. Category-level detail (structural works, electrical, plumbing, air-conditioning, kitchen fit-out, furniture, bathroom fittings, technology, finishes, signage) totals approximately ₦8,450,000 per unit before a 10% contingency, giving an indicative total of ₦9,295,000 per unit.
Do not spend money equally on every unit. Each of the 12 units should receive an individual condition grade (Section 5) once inspected, and the refurbishment specification and cost should follow that grade rather than a flat allocation. The figures above are placeholders pending that survey and should not be treated as a committed budget.
12.  Hospitality Operating Model
Guest Journey
Discover → Compare → Book → Pay → Confirm → Arrive → Check-in → Stay → Service → Check-out → Feedback → Return. Every stage should be designed deliberately rather than left informal, with measurable service standards attached (see the Operating SOPs & Governance Charter companion document for detail).
Housekeeping
A standard NRC Housekeeping SOP governs both pre-arrival preparation (cleaning, linen, toiletries, appliance and utility checks) and post-checkout process (inspection, laundry, inventory, damage assessment, restocking, readiness certification). Every unit carries a live status: Available, Reserved, Occupied, Cleaning, Inspection, Maintenance, Out of Service, Blocked.
Maintenance
A preventive maintenance schedule — covering air-conditioning, plumbing, electrical, roofing, appliances, furniture, and (if installed) generator and solar systems — replaces reactive 'wait until it breaks' management. Every unit carries a maintenance log.
Asset Protection
Each unit carries an Asset Inventory (television, refrigerator, AC, microwave, bed, dining set, sofa, each with an Asset ID) reconciled at checkout, with a transparent damage policy distinguishing normal wear, accidental minor damage, and deliberate/material damage.
Customer Service Standards
13.  Technology & Booking Platform
A digital booking system — availability calendar, pricing, booking, cancellation, extensions, check-in/out, receipts, housekeeping status, occupancy and guest history — sits at the centre of the operating architecture, subject to NRC-approved payment and banking arrangements.
Payment Principles
Bank transfer, an approved payment gateway, corporate invoicing, institutional billing or authorised POS — never a guest transferring money to a personal account.
Every booking generates an official payment reference, automatically reconciled: Booking → Invoice → Payment → Bank → Accounting → Revenue report.
Fraud & Leakage Controls
The system must be designed to detect and alert on: bookings without payment, payment without booking, discounts without authority, cancellations without approved refund, occupancy without booking, extensions without payment, cash collected but not banked, and manual rate overrides.
Cybersecurity & Data Protection
Multi-factor authentication, role-based access control, encryption, audit logs, secure payment architecture, regular vulnerability testing and backup/disaster-recovery arrangements protect guest data, payment information and management accounts, consistent with the Nigeria Data Protection Act obligations noted in Section 4.
Phased Channel Strategy
Phase 1 — NRC direct booking (website/platform).
Phase 2 — Corporate account agreements.
Phase 3 — Approved third-party booking channels, only once shown to generate incremental profit net of commission.
14.  Revenue Model
Revenue should not depend on room rates alone. The full revenue stack modelled comprises: accommodation, long-stay packages, corporate contracts, meeting/day-use charges, laundry, food & beverage, transport/transfers, event packages and other ancillary services. Ancillary revenue is modelled at 15% of room revenue — itself an indicative placeholder pending the market study.
Dynamic Pricing
Tariffs need not be flat through the year: standard rate at low demand, standard-plus-premium at normal demand, peak rate at high demand, negotiated rates for corporate accounts, discounted nightly-equivalent rates for long-stay, and an approved institutional tariff for NRC/government use where applicable. Any discount must be system-controlled and tied to an authorised role, reason and audit trail — never an informal 'I'll give you 20% off.'
Benchmarked, Not Guessed
Tariffs should be set from a market-derived price band built from comparable serviced apartments, hotels and guest houses, weekday/weekend patterns, seasonal demand, occupancy, amenities, security and transport proximity — not from an internal guess. This is why the Financial & Asset Model workbook flags every tariff cell as an indicative placeholder pending that study.
15.  Financial Model
The full financial model — Assumptions, Asset Register, CAPEX Plan, Pilot Programme Model, 5-Year Financial Model (Conservative / Base / Upside), Break-even & Investment Returns, KPI Dashboard — is provided as a companion workbook: NRC Chalet Financial & Asset Model.xlsx. This section summarises its structure and, most importantly, its limitations.
Headline Results (Base Scenario)
Gross revenue of approximately ₦117.3 million in Year 1, rising to ₦205.2 million by Year 3 (stabilised operations) and ₦239.3 million by Year 5. Net Operating Income of approximately ₦46.1 million in Year 1, rising to ₦114.5 million by Year 3. Against a total portfolio CAPEX of ₦111.5 million, the model's Base Scenario produces a Net Present Value of approximately ₦175.4 million at a 20% discount rate, an Internal Rate of Return of approximately 67%, and a simple payback period of just over one year (approximately 13 months).
Why These Numbers Must Be Treated With Caution
A roughly one-year payback and a strong double-digit IRR are, on their face, an unusually strong result for a hospitality refurbishment project. Precisely because the result looks this strong, it should be treated as a hypothesis for the pilot to test, not a figure to present to the MD as verified. Three things must happen before this model can support a capital-commitment decision:
A Quantity Surveyor's condition survey of all 12 units, replacing the placeholder ₦9,295,000-per-unit CAPEX estimate with actual costed scopes of work.
A market/competitor tariff benchmarking exercise, replacing the placeholder ₦55,000 Base ADR with a market-derived price band.
Confirmation of actual utility, staffing, security and insurance costs from NRC Estate and Finance, replacing the placeholder operating-cost assumptions.
The Pilot Programme Model tab exists for exactly this reason: to test occupancy, achievable tariff, cost-per-occupied-night, staffing needs and net margin on 5 units, at a CAPEX of approximately ₦46.5 million, before the remaining ₦65.1 million of Phase 9 CAPEX is committed.
Break-Even
Break-even occupancy in Year 1 is modelled at approximately 18% under the Base Scenario (against a modelled 40% occupancy assumption), 23% under Conservative (against 30% modelled — the narrowest margin of safety of the three scenarios), and 16% under Upside. The Conservative scenario's comparatively narrow headroom over its own break-even point is itself a signal that the pilot's early occupancy data must be watched closely before Phase 9 is triggered.
16.  Procurement Route
The commercial structure must be consistent with the Public Procurement Act, whose provisions on public property recognise modes including rental, lease, licences and tenancies, and impose formal processes around the disposal or management of public property. The Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) publishes the standard bidding documents and procurement manuals/regulations that will govern whichever route is selected.
A specific Procurement & Commercialisation Route Assessment should be completed — engaging Procurement, Legal and Property together — before any operator, manager or concessionaire is appointed under Model B, C or D (Section 9). The final instrument may be a management contract, a service contract, a concession, or another legally appropriate mechanism; this should be left for Legal, Procurement and Management to determine jointly, rather than assumed in advance as 'private management.'
17.  Governance & Internal Controls
'Revenue generation' must never become an excuse for weak public-asset governance. Every naira should be traceable through a single chain: Booking → Approved tariff → Invoice → Payment → Bank → Accounting → Revenue report → Audit. This is the detail that makes the proposal credible to Management, Finance, Procurement and Internal Audit — and it is set out in full in the companion Operating SOPs & Governance Charter document.
Project Governance Structure
Executive Sponsor — senior NRC Management.
Steering Committee — HR/Admin, Finance, Property/RPMCL as appropriate, Legal, ICT, Procurement, Internal Audit and Operations.
Project Manager — responsible for delivery.
Commercial, Estate/Property, Hospitality, Finance, Legal, Procurement, ICT and Audit/Risk Leads — each accountable for their workstream (see Section 19).
Discount & Override Governance
No staff member may grant a discount informally. Every discount requires a code, an approved tariff ceiling, a maximum discount limit, an authorised role, a stated reason and an audit trail.
Internal Audit Visibility
Internal Audit's stated responsibilities already include revenue monitoring, ensuring earnings are banked, post-audit/value-for-money review, and monitoring of NRC facilities and assets. A dedicated Internal Audit dashboard view (bookings, occupied nights, gross and banked revenue, unreconciled amounts, discount overrides, refunds, maintenance spend) should be built into the platform from launch, not added later.
18.  Risk Register
The full risk register — 16 risks with category, impact rating, mitigation and owner — is provided in the Risk Register tab of the Financial & Asset Model workbook. The critical and high-impact items are summarised below.
19.  Implementation Roadmap
Ten phases take the project from mandate to full-portfolio scale. Full detail (deliverables, indicative timing, owner and approval gate for each phase) is provided in the Implementation Roadmap tab of the Financial & Asset Model workbook.
20.  Pilot Programme
Do not spend the full CAPEX refurbishing all 12 units before knowing whether the market works. The recommended approach takes 5 representative units, makes them excellent, and tests results over a 30/60/90-day cycle before making the full investment decision.
The Ten Questions the Pilot Must Answer
Can NRC attract paying customers?
What price will customers actually accept?
What occupancy can realistically be achieved?
What does it cost to clean each room?
What does power actually cost per occupied night?
What is the real maintenance burden?
How much staff is genuinely needed?
What ancillary services actually sell?
How much net revenue remains after real costs?
Is scaling to the remaining 7 units economically rational?
The Pilot Programme Model tab of the Financial & Asset Model workbook provides a 6-month, month-by-month structure for tracking these answers against the ₦46.5 million pilot CAPEX.
21.  Key Performance Indicators
The North Star KPI is Net Revenue per Available Unit — gross revenue minus operating cost minus the appropriate asset-maintenance burden — because gross revenue alone can look impressive while the facility is quietly losing money.
22.  Approval Requirements
This document asks the Managing Director to approve, in principle, the chalet commercialisation concept as an NRC revenue-generating asset initiative, and to mandate the four immediate next steps set out in the Executive Summary (Section 1): Phase 1 discovery, constitution of a Steering Committee, appointment of an Executive Sponsor, and in-principle support for a 5-unit pilot subject to the completed business case.
Consistent with Section 4, no lease, concession, management contract or other commercial instrument is being requested for approval at this stage — only the mandate to investigate, cost and structure the opportunity properly, with the applicable Legal, Procurement, Finance and Internal Audit functions involved throughout rather than at the end.
A Note on Positioning
This proposal is deliberately structured so that NRC owns the asset, NRC approves the business model, NRC controls governance and revenue, and any operating arrangement is selected through the properly authorised and procured process. That structure protects the Corporation and gives Management room to say 'develop this further' rather than having to approve a personal operating arrangement outright.
A.  Appendices
The following materials accompany this Master Blueprint as part of the full toolkit:
Appendix A — NRC Chalet Financial & Asset Model (.xlsx): Asset Register, Assumptions, CAPEX Plan, Pilot Programme Model, 5-Year Financial Model, Break-even & Investment Returns, KPI Dashboard, Risk Register, Implementation Roadmap.
Appendix B — Draft MD Memorandum (.docx): a short covering memorandum for routing this proposal to the Managing Director.
Appendix C — Operating SOPs & Governance Charter (.docx): housekeeping SOP, guest journey standards, discount governance, Project Steering Committee charter.
Appendix D — Executive Presentation (.pptx): a summary deck for verbal presentation to the MD and Steering Committee.
Appendix E — Placeholder photography and schematic unit-layout diagram (to be replaced with actual site photography and measured drawings following the Phase 1 physical inspection).
Evidence Still Required
To convert this generic framework into an investment-grade proposal with real unit economics, the following must still be gathered and incorporated:
Exact GPS coordinates and boundary description for the Ebute Metta chalet facility.
Site photographs (exterior, interior, kitchen, bathroom) for each of the 12 units.
Measured floor plans / layout drawings for each unit.
A Quantity Surveyor's Grade A–E condition assessment for each unit.
Existing furniture and equipment inventory, where any exists.
Current or historical tariff, revenue and expense data for the facility, if any.
Electricity and water supply arrangements (grid connection, borehole, metering).
Existing security arrangements at the compound.
Any existing NRC / RPMCL documentation concerning the title, land-use status or prior commercial use of the property.
— End of Master Blueprint —

NIGERIAN RAILWAY CORPORATION
NRC CHALET ASSET COMMERCIALISATION PROGRAMME
OPERATING SOPs & GOVERNANCE CHARTER
Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos  |  12 Units
Companion to the Master Blueprint and Financial & Asset Model
1.  Housekeeping Standard Operating Procedure
This SOP governs the preparation, servicing and turnover of every NRC Executive Serviced Suite unit at Railway Compound, Ebute Metta. It applies from the day the pilot units are launched and should be reviewed after the first 90 days of operation.
1.1 Room Status States
Every unit carries one live status at all times, visible to reception, housekeeping and management:
1.2 Pre-Arrival Checklist
Room cleaned to standard (floors, surfaces, bathroom, kitchen).
Bed made; fresh linen, towels and toiletries set out.
Kitchen inspected — appliances working, basic consumables stocked.
Water, power and Wi-Fi confirmed working.
Asset inventory checked against the unit's Asset Register (Section 1.4).
Unit status moved to AVAILABLE only after supervisor inspection sign-off.
1.3 Post-Checkout Checklist
Inspection for damage or missing items against the Asset Inventory.
Laundry collected and sent for servicing.
Full clean and restocking of consumables.
Any damage or maintenance issue logged and routed to the Facilities Lead.
Readiness certification recorded before the unit returns to AVAILABLE status.
1.4 Asset Inventory & Protection
Every unit carries an asset inventory (television, refrigerator, air-conditioning unit, microwave, bed, dining set, sofa, and other fixtures), each item assigned an Asset ID. The inventory is checked at every check-in and check-out. Damage is classified and handled as follows:
2.  Guest Journey Standards
The guest journey runs: Discover → Compare → Book → Pay → Confirm → Arrive → Check-in → Stay → Service → Check-out → Feedback → Return. Each stage carries a defined standard:
2.1 Service Recovery
Every complaint becomes a tracked case: Complaint → Ticket → Category → Staff Assigned → Resolution → Guest Response → Close. This allows management to identify recurring problems rather than treating each complaint in isolation.
2.2 Guest Feedback
Feedback is tracked across cleanliness, comfort, power, water, Wi-Fi, security, location, staff, value and overall satisfaction, rolling up into a Guest Satisfaction Index tracked as a standing management KPI (see the KPI Dashboard in the Financial & Asset Model).
3.  Financial & Discount Governance
Every naira collected must be traceable through a single chain: Booking → Approved tariff → Invoice → Payment → Bank → Accounting → Revenue report → Audit. No exceptions.
3.1 Payment Principles
Guests pay only through approved channels: bank transfer, an approved payment gateway, corporate invoice, institutional billing, or authorised POS.
A guest transferring money to a personal staff account is never an approved channel, under any circumstance.
Every booking generates an official, system-issued payment reference.
3.2 Discount Governance
No staff member may grant a discount informally. Every discount requires:
A discount code.
An approved tariff ceiling.
A maximum discount limit.
An authorised role permitted to apply it.
A stated reason.
An audit trail.
3.3 Fraud & Leakage Controls
The booking and payment system must be capable of detecting and alerting management to:
Bookings without payment, or payment without a corresponding booking.
Discounts applied without authority.
Cancellations without an approved refund.
A unit shown as occupied without a corresponding booking.
Bookings extended without additional payment.
Cash collected but not banked within the required period.
Manual rate overrides outside the approved tariff structure.
3.4 Internal Audit Visibility
Internal Audit receives a dedicated, real-time dashboard view covering bookings, occupied nights, gross revenue, banked revenue, unreconciled amounts, discount overrides, refunds, and maintenance spend — consistent with Internal Audit's existing NRC-wide responsibility for revenue monitoring, ensuring earnings are banked, and post-audit / value-for-money review of NRC facilities and assets.
4.  Project Steering Committee Charter
4.1 Purpose
The Project Steering Committee provides cross-functional oversight of the NRC Chalet Asset Commercialisation Programme, ensuring that legal, financial, procurement, technology, audit and operational considerations are addressed together rather than sequentially or in isolation.
4.2 Composition
4.3 Meeting Cadence
Weekly during Phases 0–3 (mandate through business case).
Fortnightly during Phases 4–7 (design, procurement, technology build).
Weekly during Phase 8 (pilot) to track the ten pilot questions in real time.
Monthly thereafter, aligned to the KPI Dashboard reporting cycle.
4.4 Decision Gates
The Committee formally reviews and signs off at the end of each implementation phase before the next phase's spend is authorised (see the Implementation Roadmap in the Financial & Asset Model workbook for the full phase-by-phase gate structure). In particular:
End of Phase 1 — Legal opinion and asset condition findings reviewed before market study spend is authorised.
End of Phase 3 — Business case (CAPEX, OPEX, returns) formally approved before refurbishment design begins.
End of Phase 8 (Pilot) — Occupancy, service-quality, profitability and governance results reviewed before Phase 9 scale-up CAPEX is committed.
4.5 Reporting
The Committee receives, at minimum: the KPI Dashboard (financial, operational, customer, asset and governance metrics), the Risk Register with any newly identified risks, and an implementation status update against the roadmap. All reporting should draw from the live Financial & Asset Model workbook rather than from ad hoc figures.
— End of Operating SOPs & Governance Charter —

NIGERIAN RAILWAY CORPORATION
CHALET COMMERCIALISATION - EVIDENCE & MARKET VALIDATION ADDENDUM
Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos | 12 Units | Evidence Update | 4 September 2026
Internal / Restricted - Commercial-in-Confidence
1. Executive finding
The previous draft had the right business shape but several statements were too easy to challenge because they were based on placeholders or broad market claims. Current research supports a stronger, more defensible pitch: NRC has a documented commercial hospitality precedent at the same Ebute-Metta compound; current local competitors visibly price hotel rooms around N27,500-N55,000/night; current Yaba one-bedroom short-let listings show a much wider serviced-apartment band, including N65,000-N130,000/day examples and a portal-reported average of N120,000/day. The correct conclusion is not that NRC can charge N55,000 or N120,000. The correct conclusion is that a N55,000 working Base ADR is plausible enough to test, while the final tariff must be established through a controlled local benchmark and pilot.
2. What is now corroborated
Same-compound NRC precedent
In September 2021, NRC opened a 40-bed commercial Railway Guest House at its Ebute-Metta station. NAN reporting put the project cost at about N320 million and stated that Ojez Group was selected from more than 30 bidders to manage the facility. This is the strongest narrative anchor for the proposal because it demonstrates that NRC has already used the basic model of commercialising hospitality assets at this location. It does not prove that the 12 chalets will perform similarly.
Current Ojez price ladder
Hotels.ng currently lists Ojez Hotel & Suites in Ebute Metta from N27,500 to N55,000 per night across several room categories. The Ojez company website still identifies O’JEZ Hotels & Suites as part of its hospitality business and places an operating contact at the Railway Recreation Center, Ebute-Metta.
Current Yaba serviced-apartment market
Nigeria Property Centre currently shows 110 one-bedroom short-let listings in Yaba as of 4 September 2026, with a portal-reported average of N120,000/day. Individual observed furnished/serviced examples include N65,000/day in Alagomeji and N130,000/day on Muritala Muhammed Way. These are asking/listing prices, not audited achieved revenue.
Lagos market scale
Edala Development research, as reported by Nairametrics, estimated Lagos short-let market revenue at N281.03bn in 2025 from 6,398 tracked units. The report describes a maturing market with continuing demand but increasing competition and supply.
Occupancy evidence
A September 2026 Nairametrics report quoted Edala Development’s COO as saying occupancy across Edala properties ranges from about 59% to 80%, with stronger demand in December-February. The same report states that industry-wide data are limited. Therefore the prior statement that Lagos shortlets “average 51% occupancy” should be removed unless a primary source is obtained.
3. What should be removed or softened from the earlier draft
“Lagos shortlet occupancy citywide averages around 51%.” - REMOVE. Current evidence found does not substantiate this as an industry-wide Lagos average.
“The ₦55,000 Base ADR is verified.” - DO NOT SAY THIS. Say it is a working hypothesis supported by the local price ladder and to be validated by a formal benchmark and pilot.
“Renovation costs are ₦150,000-₦250,000 per sqm.” - DO NOT use as the project’s cost basis. Online construction/renovation guides are too generic; the business case should use a measured QS BOQ. Current new-build cost commentary shows wide variation by specification, which reinforces the need for a project-specific BOQ.
“40%-60% occupancy is conservative against the Lagos average.” - REFRAME. It is a planning scenario that should be tested against the pilot; it is not directly benchmarked to a verified citywide statistic.
4. Recommended evidence-backed planning assumptions
5. Plain-English meaning of the financial terms
ADR: Average Daily Rate: the average price charged for one occupied unit for one night.
Occupancy: The percentage of available nights actually sold.
CAPEX: One-time investment to renovate, equip and prepare the units.
OPEX: Recurring running costs: staff, power, water, housekeeping, security, internet, maintenance, etc.
NOI: Net Operating Income: operating revenue less operating costs, before financing and other corporate-level items defined in the model.
Break-even occupancy: The occupancy level at which operating revenue covers the modelled operating cost base.
Payback: How long the incremental cash generation would take to recover the renovation investment under the specified assumptions.
NPV: Net Present Value: today’s value of future cash flows after applying a discount rate for time and risk.
IRR: Internal Rate of Return: the discount rate that makes the project’s NPV equal to zero; it is a return metric, not a guaranteed interest rate.
Management contract: NRC retains ownership and hires a professional operator to run the facility for a defined contractual fee / arrangement.
Concession: A longer-term commercial arrangement that can transfer more operating rights/control to a private party and therefore requires more careful legal/procurement structuring.
6. What the MD should hear - not a technical lecture
“NRC already has a precedent at this exact compound: the Railway Guest House was commercialised and professionally managed. I am proposing that we investigate whether the 12 existing chalets can be converted into a smaller serviced-accommodation product. I am not asking Management to approve a lease or hand over the asset. I am asking for permission to inspect the property, establish the legal route, benchmark the market, cost the renovation properly and test five units. If the numbers work, Management decides whether to scale.”
7. Evidence discipline for the next revision
Use “listed/asking price” whenever referring to portal rates. Do not call listing prices “market achieved rates.”
Use the same-compound NRC/Ojez precedent as evidence of organisational feasibility, not evidence of financial performance for the chalets.
Use the current Yaba listing data to support a price-range discussion, not a promise of tariff.
Use actual pilot bookings, occupancy, costs and guest feedback to replace scenario assumptions after launch.
Replace all renovation placeholders with a measured Quantity Surveyor BOQ and contractor market testing before capital approval.
8. Sources

### DOCUMENT: `06_SUPPORTING_MEDIA/NRC_Chalet_Evidence_Validation_Pack_2026__EXTRACTED/NRC_Chalet_Plain_English_MD_Pitch_Guide.docx`

**Size:** 40,178 bytes  
**SHA-256:** `05a77cabf8a4a94aaf85ff9c827a89ebf5ae7c3c0f58c2fc33eb21825b60036c`

NIGERIAN RAILWAY CORPORATION
NRC CHALET - PLAIN-ENGLISH MD PITCH & QUESTION PREPARATION GUIDE
Railway Compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos | 12 Units | Evidence Update | 4 September 2026
Internal / Restricted - Commercial-in-Confidence
1. The idea in one sentence
“Take 12 NRC chalet units in Ebute Metta that currently need renovation, test whether five can be converted into professionally managed one-bedroom serviced suites, and only scale if the pilot proves demand, service quality, governance and net revenue.”
2. Why this is not just an idea
NRC has a documented precedent at the same compound. In September 2021, the Corporation opened a 40-bed commercial Railway Guest House at Ebute-Metta and selected Ojez Group from more than 30 bidders to manage it. That is evidence of organisational precedent. It is not proof that the chalets will make money; the pilot must prove that.
3. The three numbers you should be ready to explain
Why ₦55,000 per night? Because current Ojez hotel listings in Ebute Metta extend up to ₦55,000/night, while current furnished/serviced one-bedroom Yaba listings include ₦65,000 and ₦130,000/day examples. ₦55,000 is therefore a testable working hypothesis for a fully equipped one-bedroom suite, not a final tariff.
Why 40% occupancy in Year 1? It is a deliberately moderate planning scenario, not a claim about Lagos. Current industry-wide occupancy data are weak. We will test actual occupancy with five pilot units.
Why ₦111.5m CAPEX? It is a placeholder model output based on an assumed per-unit renovation amount. It is not a QS estimate. No capital decision should rely on it until the 12 units are surveyed and a BOQ is produced.
4. Questions the MD may ask - and how to answer
What evidence says people will pay? Current comparable listings show an observable local price ladder from approximately ₦27,500 hotel rooms in the same area to ₦65,000-₦130,000 examples for furnished/serviced one-bedroom units in Yaba. The pilot converts this into actual demand evidence.
Why should NRC do this instead of leasing the property? The first question is not lease versus operate. The first question is which legally permissible model gives NRC the best combination of control, risk and net revenue. Four models should be compared before selection.
What stops revenue leakage? A digital booking-to-bank chain: booking, approved tariff, invoice, payment, bank, accounting, revenue report and audit. No informal staff discounts and no personal accounts.
What if the market does not respond? The five-unit pilot is the protection. NRC commits to testing first and scaling only after a formal gate.
What about legal/procurement issues? No lease, concession or management contract is being requested at this stage. Legal, Estate/RPMCL, Procurement and Finance first determine the permissible commercial route.
Why not renovate all 12 now? Because the business case is still uncertain. A pilot preserves capital discipline and produces real operating data before full rollout.
5. The jargon translated
ADR: Average Daily Rate: the average price charged for one occupied unit for one night.
Occupancy: The percentage of available nights actually sold.
CAPEX: One-time investment to renovate, equip and prepare the units.
OPEX: Recurring running costs: staff, power, water, housekeeping, security, internet, maintenance, etc.
NOI: Net Operating Income: operating revenue less operating costs, before financing and other corporate-level items defined in the model.
Break-even occupancy: The occupancy level at which operating revenue covers the modelled operating cost base.
Payback: How long the incremental cash generation would take to recover the renovation investment under the specified assumptions.
NPV: Net Present Value: today’s value of future cash flows after applying a discount rate for time and risk.
IRR: Internal Rate of Return: the discount rate that makes the project’s NPV equal to zero; it is a return metric, not a guaranteed interest rate.
Management contract: NRC retains ownership and hires a professional operator to run the facility for a defined contractual fee / arrangement.
Concession: A longer-term commercial arrangement that can transfer more operating rights/control to a private party and therefore requires more careful legal/procurement structuring.
6. What not to say
“The project will make ₦114m NOI by Year 3.” Say instead: “The current model indicates that outcome under the placeholder Base Scenario; we need to validate the tariff, costs and occupancy.”
“Lagos occupancy is 51%.” Do not use unless a primary source is obtained.
“Renovation will cost ₦9.3m per unit.” Say: “The current model carries ₦9.295m per unit as a placeholder; the QS BOQ will replace it.”
“Ojez proves we will succeed.” Say: “Ojez proves NRC has already used a commercial hospitality model at the same compound.”
7. Your 30-second close
“I am not asking you to commit NRC to a hotel business today. I am asking for permission to properly investigate an existing asset that is currently under-used. We already have a precedent for commercial hospitality at Ebute-Metta. Let us inspect the 12 units, establish the legal and procurement route, benchmark the market, cost five units properly and run a controlled pilot. If the evidence says it works, Management can then decide whether to scale.”

## 7. Consolidated continuity index

This section is an index of the major state and decisions already captured by the source documents in the kit. The detailed source corpus above remains authoritative.

**Phase 4 architecture:** Global Job Intelligence Engine beginning with remote-work discovery; Nigeria-first and globally extensible; long-term Opportunity Intelligence → Career Intelligence → Problem-Solving Intelligence.

**Main gates:** G0 through G12 remain the controlling gate sequence. Current state in the kit: G0–G8 complete/evidenced; G9 in progress; G10/G11/G12 not started.

**G9 current position:** G9.4 Native Opportunity Engine is evidenced and closed. G9.5 Canonical Backend/API Integration is in architecture/security inspection; public deployment is not yet approved.

**Public/private boundary:** PDE OS control-plane source must remain private. Public website may consume only approved public-safe projections; private CRM/finance/operations/audit data and secrets must not be exposed.

**PDE OS source discovery:** Actual Apps Script project contains QueryEngine plus G310–G320 opportunity-intelligence modules, operational CRM/lead/Drive/Gmail/Health/Logger code, tests and fixtures.

**Existing web endpoints:** Health.js contains doGet(); Leads.js contains doPost(). The existing doPost() writes to the private LEADS spreadsheet through createLead(), so it is not a suitable public Opportunity Engine endpoint.

**Canonical query path:** buildQueryPlan(inputs) → generateQueryPlan(inputs), with explicit geography/worldwide controls, downstream eligibility/verification requirements, and application automation prohibited.

**Website deployment:** Cloudflare branch preview deployment succeeded on the G9 branch after adding wrangler.jsonc. Production was not merged/promoted at the documented stopping point.

**Git migration:** A local clone of the Apps Script project was created for private GitHub migration. .gitignore correctly excludes local credential material such as .clasprc.json, while .clasp.json and appsscript.json are retained.

**No recognizable credentials:** The recognizable credential-pattern scan returned no matches. Keyword scans did find intentional security-test strings/fixtures such as SECRET-DO-NOT-LEAK; those are not automatically evidence of real credentials.

Do not deploy the existing PDE OS web app publicly until a safe public API boundary has been designed, tested and verified.
